 1 SDX-5 Overview

There have been eight wells drilled to the primary reservoirs on the Shah Deniz structure. These are SDX-1,
2, 3 and 4 and their sidetracks, plus SDA-01, -02, -03Z and -04.

SDX-5 (BF27) well is planned to be drilled to the “Known Reservoirs” (ie Bal VIIIC, SP2, SP3 & SP4) in the
South East Sector of the Shah Deniz Field. The well designation, SDX-5 (BF27), follows the convention of
being the  fifth exploration/appraisal well on the structure to a target location designated BF27. The well
location is shown below in Figure 1.



                     ! " #(

                             Figure 1 Location of SDX-5 (BF27) Well


The well design has been based on the technical success and integrity demonstrated on SDX-4.

    •   Well through the ‘known’ reservoir intervals only targeting the Balakhany VIIIC, SP2, SP3 & SP4
    •   Single well to an updip gas location and will not be sidetracked to pre-planned alternative
        location
    •   Appraisal well which has been designed as a keeper
    •    1st Well in South East sector of the field leading to pore/frac uncertainty
    •

2 SDX-5 Well Objectives

2.1  SDX-5 Well Objectives

2.1.1  Strategic Well Objectives

  •    No accidents, no harm to people, no damage to the environment.
  •    To provide  sufficient reservoir information  to support the Stage 2 development [For known
         reservoirs: Balakhany VIII, Balakhany X (SP2), Fasila B (SP3), Fasila D (SP4)]
  •    To provide drillability assurance for Stage 2 drilling program


2.1.2 HSE Objectives

  •     Deliver BP safety performance metrics for wells related activity. (SOC, FOCUS  , Safety/ Rep
        Audits, etc)
  •      Full compliance with BP discharge requirements.
  •      Full compliance with PSA HSE requirements.


2.1.3  Technical Well Objectives

  The technical well objectives are prioritized as follows:

  1.    Evaluate the GIIP estimates for the East Flank; reservoir quality, static pressure communication to
     SW area and Stage 1 area.
  2.    Evaluate reservoir productivity, connectivity and fluids from tests.
  3.    Evaluate surface hole drillability in the deep water to the South East of Shah Deniz.
  4.   Reduce uncertainty in the south east Shah Deniz development drillability, pore pressure, wellbore
          stability and fracture pressure, particularly in the Surakhany and Sabunchi horizons.
  5.    Retain well as a production well.
  6.   Reduce seismic depth uncertainty.


2.1.4  Performance Objectives
  •     Acquire all programmed minimum data.
  •       Drill and evaluate the well in better than Pmean days per 10,000 feet (97.6 days/10K). Target
         better than Pmean days (310 days) for drilling and evaluating the well.
  •     Carry out well planning and execution consistent with BP common process.

3.3  Final Well TD Criteria

  The stratigraphy to top SP5 shale is expected to be similar to the SDX-4Y well. The TD criteria for
  SDX-5 is a 20m logging sump below the Base Fasila D (SP4). The Fasila D (SP4) reservoir is
  prognosed at 6548 mMDbrt (5907 mTVDss) +/- 200m error bar. The 20m logging sump will be required
   to allow full evaluation of the reservoir (refer to Shah Deniz Development Technical File Note SDX-5 TD
  Logging Sump Ver 1.1). The risk of drilling into potentially high pressures beneath the Fasila D is
   present (this interval was penetrated in the appraisal leg of the SDX-4 well) but will be minimized through
   real time pore Pressure detection as well as a short logging sump. Base Fasila D (SP4) will be
   confirmed by combination of LWD data, lithology data and pore pressure data.


    Prognosed TD data  (20m below Base Fasila D)

3.5  Geothermal Temperature

  The predicted geothermal temperature profile at the SDX-5 location was extracted from the Shah Deniz
  3D basin model.

  The likely range for seawater surface temperatures is between 27°C and 6°C. Temperatures at mid
   water depth range from 7.3°C to 6.7°C and temperatures at mud line range from 7°C to 5°C.

   At a planned TD of 5946m TVDbrt (5924m TVDss) the temperature is predicted to be 100.4°C (212.7°F).

Pore/Fracture Pressure
SDX-5 (BF27) will be drilled in the South-eastern area of the field, which may form a new segment
(potentially cut off from Stage 1 location by an East to West lineation seen on seismic at the SP4 level).
Whilst the general stratigraphy and pressure profile is expected to be similar down to the base of Fasila D
(SP4), surprises such as the unpredicted isolated Fasila C sand encountered in SDX-4X cannot be
ruled out.
Shallow PP/FG (down to 22” shoe)
Pore pressure and fracture gradient (PPFG) analyses were conducted at the SDX-05 well location. The used
PPFG model was verified with pressure measurements (MDTs at SDA-01, SDA-02 and SDX-4) as well as
drilling observations (LoTs and kicks at SDA-01, SDA-02, SDX-2, SDX-3, and SDX-4) and excellent
agreements between the predicted and observed PPFG values were observed. The verified/calibrated model
was used to predict a lower and an upper bound PPFG values at the SDX-05 well location.
The pre-drill plans for drilling and cementing were developed taking the lower bound PPFG into account.
However, it is also likely that the upper bound PPFG will be encountered and, therefore, potential risks and
mitigation were also considered in the well plan.
Deep PP/FG (below 22” shoe)
The first anticipated pressure ramp occurs between the first and second Surakhany anhydrite (between Top
Surakhany and the se220 pick). The pressures are predicted to increase from 1.4 sg to 1.6 sg.
     Note: This ramp actually starts higher and is more gradual than shown on the plot where the ramp is
      abrupt and starts at the se220 pick. The projected SDX-4 MDT pressure point at 2621m TVDBRT (1.46
      sg) highlights this.
The second major pressure ramp occurs below the Top Sabunchi shale around 4450m TVDBRT where the
pressure is expected to increase from 1.8 sg to 1.9 sg.
Below Top Balakhany, the pressures are expected to decrease gradually from 1.9sg to 1.57 sg before
entering the reservoir section.
A 20m logging sump will be drilled below base Fasila D (SP4) before reaching TD. There is a potential risk for
the high pressured SP5 sand encountered in SDX-4Y to be present at the SDX-5 (BF27) location, and
although this sand should not be reached by this well, there is still a risk of doing so.
    •     If sand encountered within upper 17m TVD SP5 shale maximum likely pressure 15600 psi   1.84
      sg @ 5924m TVDSS (13763psi + (93psi/m*20m))
    •  Maximum predicted pressure if sand in SP5 shale is not encountered: 14000 psi   1.76 sg @
      5581m TVDSS (SP1 pressure).
    •   Potential pressures if the well were to intersect the equivalent sand as seen in SDA-01 (positioned ~
      [60m - 90m] below base SP4): 18120 psi   2.00 sg @ 5938m TVDSS.
    •   Potential pressures if the well were to intersect the SP5 equivalent sand (or one connected to it) as
       seen in SDX-4Y: 17915   2.13 sg @ 5927m TVDSS  (value of 18074 psi @ 6035m TVDSS taken
      up along a water gradient to 5927m TVDSS). The pressure seen in the SP5 interval in the SDX-4Y
        well was 18615psi.
Model Summary
A three dimensional deterministic pore pressure-fracture pressure cube has been built, assuming layer
connectivity over the crest and using sonic log data (for shale pressure), influxes and MDT’s (for sand
pressure) from the exploration wells (SDX-1Y, SDX-2Y, SDX-3X) and the pre-drill wells (SDA-01, SDA-02,
SDA-03Z, SDA_04) to model and predict pore and shale fracture pressure variation at Shah Deniz. The
deterministic sand pressures are modelled to be the worst expected pressures (max encountered
overpressure in a section applied to an artificial sand layer in this section), except in the reservoir section
where they are modelled to be the most likely pressures due to the abundance of overlapping pressure data
from all the wells. The risk of hitting an unpredicted and isolated sand can not be ruled out though;
whether this is for the overburden or the reservoir section.
The shale fracture gradient model is less well constrained (scarce LOT data) than the pore pressure and is
therefore more prone to deviate from the prediction. The SDX-5 (BF27) trajectory should offer a wide enough
drilling window (space between the PP and FP curve) in the zones where FP is more uncertain (below Top
Balakhany due to a more sandy lithology and tectonic stress).

 7 Primary and Contingency Operations

Best efforts have been made to ensure that this drilling program complies with all applicable BP and Business
Unit (BU) policies, as well as, all governmental legislations/ policies.

Priority for safety while drilling SDX-5 shall be in the following order of importance:

    1.  Personnel
    2.  Environment
    3.  The Installation
    4.  Reservoir Integrity
    5.  Well Delivery

The operational procedures in this document should be read in conjunction with the following documents. The
order of hierarchy is as listed below.

    1. BP Drilling and Wells Operations Policy (Issue 5; May 2003)
    2.  SDX-5 Section Specific Management of Change documents (MOC)

Notes:

This program has principally been written to cover SDX-5 primary operations down through the setting of the
13-3/8” x 13-5/8” casing. There will be further programs issued as the SDX-5 operation progress, these
being:

     •   12-1/4” Hole thru 7-5/8” x 5-1/2” Production Liner
     •  DST Program
     •   Suspension Program
     •   Contingency Programs (as required)


DIMS Phasing is incorporated into the primary operational sequence [blue text].  If any of the three
contingency liners are run the DIMS phasing will change.

 7.1  Primary Operational Sequence

    7.1.1  Rig Move    [PRE]

1)  Move rig to SDX-5 location as per co-ordinates detailed below and verify coordinates with Fugro surveyor
   and BP Marine.

 SDX-5 Proposed Surface Location:               Lat 039° 48’ 45.264” N  Long 050° 31’ 41.458” E
 (Modified Gauss Kruger Zone 9N)                                                   Easting: 459 599 mE    Northing: 4 408 903 mN

Notes:

    •  A Safety Stand Down and Pre-Spud meeting will be performed on the rig prior to spud
    •    Drilling Reps will perform a rig (safety) inspection prior to commencement of drilling operations.
    •   The BOP stack will be stump tested to 10,000psi except for the Annulars which will be tested to 7000psi
      (70% of 10K psi rating) prior to running.
    •   Coordinate emergency response  drills as directed (Rig Abandonment, Med-evac, Incident Response,
       Muster Drill and Shallow Gas)
    •   Refer to the Istiglal Mooring Analysis completed by Transocean for SDX-5 (Revision 1, April 7th 2008). Rig
       heading planned for 45deg clockwise from North and a 30-60deg mooring pattern. Measured clockwise
        from the Bow the line headings are 30, 60, 120, 150, 210, 240, 300 and 330. Initial line tension is 220Kips.
    •  Once 4 primary anchors are deployed and the rig is ballasted to drilling draft commence deployment of
     ROV for 70m seabed survey and begin pre-spud operations.
    •  Once anchored on location a full winch off drill will be conducted with all crews participating
    •   At the final well location, the mooring system should be checked by pre-tensioning the anchors to a value
          for a period agreed with the drilling contractor.
    •   Record anchor line tensions and lengths in DIMS.
    •  A shallow hazards assessment (“Shallow Hazard Assessment, SDX-5 Appraisal Well Shah Deniz PSA
       Area Offshore Azerbaijan” – Mark Hobson 08/03/07) has noted the following:

        This section presents highlights of the information included in the Shallow Geohazard Assessment (SGA)
       document which was produced in March of 2007.   It should be noted that some of the recommendations
        included in the SGA document and presented in this section are considered not applicable/valid and have
       been updated based on the results of pore pressure analyses which were performed in April of 2008.

       Shallow Gas
            • ML to depth of 1320m TVDBRT - identified no instances of shallow gas accumulations within a
           300m radius of the well location. Therefore the risk of encountering a shallow gas accumulation is
              considered to be Negligible.
            • 1320m TVDBRT to 1523m TVDBRT (+/-51m) – small amplitude anomaly will be intersected at
           1452m TVDBRT (+/-47m).  This is below the 22” casing shoe so will be drilled with weighted mud
            and BOPs. The risk of encountering a shallow gas accumulation in this interval is considered to be
            Low.

       Shallow Faults
            • No faults have been identified within a 300m radius of the well trajectory from the seabed in the
               extent of the shallow section (1500m TVDSS +/-51m).

       Running Sands / Flowing Sands / Over-pressured Water Sands
            • The running sands interval has caused problems with wellbore stability in a number of offset wells.
                 In SDX-1 and SDX-3 the lowest identified sand caused drilling problems by flowing into the hole.
            The ROV also observed a strong flow of water with associated gas from this interval. In SDX-4 the
               section was drilled with a 28” liner in place and no problems were encountered.  The ‘Running
              Sands’, which have provided a source for shallow water flow and gas in offset wells, are predicted
                  in the interval 834±18m and 911±22m TVDSS. SDX-5 will take a similar approach to SDX-4 and
               therefore a 28” liner will be set prior to drilling this interval (set above the top of the error bar), so the
                  risk of wellbore stability from the running sands is considered Low.  It should be noted that this
             recommendation has been updated based on the results of pore pressure analyses which indicated
                that the pore pressure profile at SDX-5 is different from that at SDX-4 and, consequently, hole
                  instability and potential flows are considered to be a LIKELY RISK in the SDX-5 well.
     Shah Deniz D&C                       SDX-5 Operations Drilling Program                       Rev1.04

            • Throughout the remainder of the tophole section, to the limit of this investigation at 1500±51m
          TVDSS (1805ms TWT), the risk of shallow water flow development is considered to be Negligible.

       Unconsolidated / Weak / Flowing Layers
            • There is a Low probability of tight hole conditions while drilling the Palaeo flow deposits, which
              occur at eight levels within the shallow section down to the 22” casing point.
            • There is also a Low risk of encountering flowing sands within the ‘Running Sands’ interval which
                    will be encountered between 834±18m and 911±22m TVDSS.

      Mud Volcanoes & Mud Flows
            • Two active mud volcanoes occur within the Shah Deniz area. These are 8km NW of SDX-5
                location and 12km to WSW. There is considered to be negligible risk of flows from these reaching
               the SDX-5 location.

       Anchoring - Ammunition Dump
            • The northern limit of the Navy Prohibited area number 36 is 1.4km south of the location. An ROV
              survey of any anchor locations within the area of the ammunition dump should be made. Refer to
             Unexploded Ordinance (UXO) Risk Management Plan for SDX-5 for further detail.

      Gas Hydrates
            • There are no indications of gas hydrates at or in the vicinity of the proposed SDX-5 location and the
                  risk of encountering hydrates along the well trajectory is considered to be Negligible.

    •   The Shah Deniz field presents no H2S hazards based on the DST data and current production ongoing at
        the SD platform. A coupon run at SDA-4 showed a trace of H2S at 0.02 ppm which is absorbed into the
        metal of the casing or drillpipe and will never been seen at surface.
    •  AGR Riserless Mud Recovery (RMR) System installation (for use on 26 x 28” hole section and as
        contingency for 26” x 32” hole section) will take approximately 7 days with an AGR crew of six people. As
      much prep as practical will be done prior to reaching SDX-5 location (dependent upon Istiglal work scope
         prior to SDX-5 spud).
    •   Prior to running the BOP’s, confirm the ram configuration is as follows from top down:
                   •   Blind / Shear Rams
                   •   5” x 7” Variable Bore Rams
                   •   5” Fixed Pipe Rams
                   •   3-1/2” x 5-1/2” Variable Bore Rams
    •    Full mudlogging service required; 12 person crew with 3 personnel per 12hour shift (Data Engineer,
        Mudlogger, Sample Catcher). Formation evaluation log (FEL), Pressure evaluation log (PEL), Drilling
        Evaluation Log (DEL) and Gas Ratio Log (GRL) should be prepared at Wellsite to BP standards from spud
         to TD of the well.
    •   High resolution Gas Chromatography will be required (RESERVAL or equivalent) over the Balakhany
        sections to TD. Gas traps in both active pits and shakers will be required to remove the effect of re-
         circulated gas. The GCMS (Flair system) will NOT be used on this well.


OPERATIONAL ALERT – Mud Weights

The well design is based on down hole mud weight (DHMW) and the well will be drilled according to DHMW. The
mud density required at any point in time will depend upon prevailing hole conditions and therefore must be
adjusted accordingly. Hydraulic modeling has taken into account effects of down hole temperature and pressure on
Synthetic Based Mud (SBM) density.

Specified surface mud weights (SMW), as measured in the mud balance, must not be confused with down hole
mud weight (DHMW) which will be taken with a pressure balance and monitored with PWD sensors. All DHMWs
stated in the program are based on DHMW at section TD.

    •   26” x 42” and 26” x 32” hole sections density should be based on SMW
    •   26” x 28” hole section, a dual gradient will be in effect using the Riserless Mud Recovery (RMR) system.
    •   17-1/2” x 22”, 16 ½”, 12 ¼“ and 8½” hole section densities should be based on PWD data = DHMW.

7.1.2  26”x 42” Hole, 36” Casing (Riserless) [PRE changing to COND1]

  7.1.2.1  Section Objectives / TD Criteria

•   Set 9 joints of 36” casing vertically in the lower shallow soils, both to support long heavy strings on
     this well and to reach a competent formation for the surface casing for subsequent over-pressured
    sections.
•   Target depth is 660m MDBRT (depth picked to accommodate conductor tally)
•   Provide 3m stick-up of the LPH.
•  Land LP Housing at less than 1 deg
•  No slump of conductor when released
•   Fully cemented to mudline

  7.1.2.2  Hole Section Discussion / Risks / Mitigation

 •    Within this hole section, the predicted lower bound “planned” pore pressure is 1.00 sg while the
      predicted upper bound “worst case” pore pressure is equivalent to or near the fracture gradient.
 •    This hole section will be drilled with seawater.
 •    This hole section will be drilled underbalanced and the fizz gas zone may be penetrated close to
      section TD which could result in hole instability or fizz gas.  No permeable sands have been
      reported in the SGA within this interval.
 •   The base plan is to displace the well with a 1.30 sg water based mud for stability.  If hole instability
      and/or fizz gas are observed, then there is an option to increase the Pad mud from 1.30 sg to 1.45
     sg prior to running the conductor casing.
 •    Tight Hole Conditions:
          o  Based on previous drilling experiences in other SDX wells, there is a Low probability of
                    tight hole conditions whilst drilling the Palaeo flow deposits located from 563m +/-3m
              TVDbrt to 614m +/-6m TVDbrt.
 •   Washout / Crater at mudline:
          o  Commence drilling with low WOB (2-5,000lbs), 40 - 60 rpm and 800 gpm, until 42” hole
               opener is 5m below mudline
 •     Fill in OH preventing conductor from reaching desired depth
          o  Confirm available rathole length on wiper trip
          o  Option to increase pad mud from 1.30 sg to 1.45 sg
 •   Conductor deviation is greater than 1 deg from vertical
          o    Drill section with high RPM to sustain vertical
          o  Totco Survey to verify hole deviation prior to running casing
 •    Failure to lift quality cement to seabed (wash out, cratering tendency on top section)
 •    Failure to detect cement at seabed.
 •   Slump of conductor upon release.
          o   Mitigations for the above 3x risks include:
                   Use 200% annular excess
                   Add red dye and mica to the preflush
                 Pump a top up job
                   Add CemNET fibers to tail slurry

  7.1.2.3  Planning / Preparation

•    Drill string: ~660m 5” S135 19.5ppf
•   Landing string: ~550m 5” S135 19.5ppf
•   Ensure permits are in place for the over the side work planned for this interval.
•  A Retrievable Guide Base will not be used. The BOP is fitted with a down funnel.
•  The 36” RL-4RB Lifting Clamps will be installed on the conductor in town. Check for transportation
   damage.
•  Vetco will provide drawings of MS-700 Fullbore-2 Wellhead System with serial numbers and
   have a Rep offshore. Vetco Rep and BP WSL to verify FB-2 LP Housing prior to running.
•  The primary 36” Fullbore-2 LP Housing Assembly will be M/U in town by Vetco and will consist of:

    •   Record all serial numbers on BHA components and measurement from bottom of 42” cutter to nose
         of 26” bit
    •  A non-ported float valve will be used in the BHA
    •   Paint the bit, hole opener and first drill collar yellow to aid visibility with ROV.
    •   Strap pipe prior to RIH.
    •  Space out to drill a complete stand after tagging bottom / seabed
    •   Ensure Remote Operated Vehicle (ROV) observes last ~ 30m and tagging of seabed
    •  Due to the potential of poor visibility generated by silt clouds once drilling commences ROV should
        layout all marker buoys and sand bags prior to spud.

3)  Tag seabed, pumps off.  Perform penetration test to 10klbs. Record the following on IADC & DIMS
    reports: [COND1]
    •  RTE to water level (air gap) at drilling draft
    •  RTE to Mud Line (where bit takes weight)
    •   Water Depth
    •    Drilling Draft
    •   Penetration depth w/ 10klbs Weight on bit (WOB)
    •   Flag anchor winch lines and record well center

4)   Drill 26” x 42” vertical hole riserless to +/- 665m tvdbrt with Seawater (1.03SG SMW) and Pre-Hydrated
    Bentonite (PHB) sweeps.

    •   Position ROV on the seabed and monitor open hole and returns closely with the ROV.
    •  No hot work or non essential personnel on deck while drilling surface hole.
    •   Position standby boat upwind/up current prior to spud.
    •  Commence drilling with low WOB (2-5klbs), 40 - 60 rpm and 800 gpm, until 42” hole opener is 5m
       below mudline, to ensure that the hole is drilled vertical and to prevent a crater at the seabed.
    •   Stage up rotary to 90 – 120 rpm and 1200gpm as dictated by string whip – maintain rotary as high as
        possible to minimise hole angle. Stage up pumps to avoid a washout.
    •  Pump 60bbl PHB sweeps every half stand.  More frequent  if conditions dictate (hole condition,
         flowrate, ROP, returns observed). At connections spot 60 bbl sweep on bottom.
    •  TD should allow for a 5m rat hole beneath the 36” casing.
    •   At section TD, pump ~150-200 bbl PHB sweep & circulate out while working the pipe.
    •  When using seawater and sweeps VH indicates the transition to POOR hole cleaning will occur at 10
       meters per hour and 1200 gpm. The frequency and the size of sweeps will be dictated by the ROP
      and volume of fluid being pumped. Monitor returns closely with the ROV.

    42” Hole Section Hydraulics: Bit  : 26in Y11C, Bit Nozzles: 3 x 24, 1 x 20 center, TFA=1.632,
    Baker 42in HO: Nozzles, 3 x 20, 3 x 16, TFA=1.509
    Based on ROP of 10m/hr
    Flow Rate (gpm)           1200                1300                  1400

   SPP (psi)                 753                 848                   947

   ESD mudline               1.023                  1.023                   1.023

   ESD td                    1.025                  1.025                   1.025

   VH ECD shoe              1.023                  1.023                   1.023

   VH ECD TD                1.035                  1.034                   1.032

                    42” Drilling Parameter Acceptable Ranges
     Circulation Rate (gpm)    1200 -1400 (800gpm to start spud, see notes above)
    Max WOB (klb)         15K for 1st 3 stands, 25K once below 640m MDbrt
   RPM                   90-140 (50 RPM for spud)
    Max ROP (m/hr)         10 - 15

[ صفحه 31 از 160 ]
────────────────────────────────────────────
         Data Acquisition: 42” Hole for 36” Conductor (from Setting Depth to Mud Line)
     Wireline                                    None
     Survey                              TOTCO
   MWD / LWD                                None


5)  Displace hole to 1.30sg Pad mud (Cl diluted <21,000ppm to allow discharge to sea). Option to make
     light treatment of LCM in displacement fluid of 3 ppb of G Seal, 3 ppb of Durcal 130, and 3 ppb of Safe
   Carb Z2, and 3 ppb Safe-Carb Z3.

6)  Perform 15 minute flow check with ROV for indications of swabbed gas.

7)  Drop Totco survey

8)  Pull out of hole to +/-10m below seabed (~560m BRT).

    •  Pump mud equal to steel displacement through Drillpipe (DP)
    •     If any tight spots are observed, attempt to wash through prior to backreaming.
    •  Be aware the hole may relax or swell a little, which may result in a flow signal at the seabed with the
      ROV.
    •   Allow time for ROV to mark well with Grimsby Buoys
    •   Let the hole relax for one hour
    •   Recover Totco survey while resting the hole.

9)  After an hour, run back to bottom to check hole condition.

    •   36” Conductor will be set at 660mTVDbrt (110m below ML – 3m stick up above ML for the LPH)
    •     If fill is less than 2m, pull out of hole to run 36” conductor.
    •     If fill is more than 2m, pump 100-150 bbl Hi-Vis sweep, followed by kill weight (1.45sg) Pad Mud to
        displace the hole and repeat the wiper trip. No requirement to increase Pad Mud above 1.45 sg
        since the worst case pore pressure could be close  to overburden  (i.e. pad mud weight not
        achievable).
    •     If the Totco survey showed greater than 1.0 deg inclination at section TD, work the hole with the hole
       opener to TD and repeat the Totco survey.

10) POOH to run conductor

    •  Pump mud equal to steel displacement through Drillpipe (DP)
    •  Rack back BHA prior to picking up conductor

      7.1.2.6  36in Conductor Running Operations       [COND1]

1)  Run 36” 374ppf, X-52, RL4-RB, 1in wall thickness casing as per tally.

    •  Review and update Job Risk Assessments (JRA’s).
    •   Ensure two Vetco reps are offshore
    •   Hold pre job safety meeting (PJSM) prior to picking up Conductor
    •   Ensure horizontal lines painted every meter on the welded float shoe joint for ROV to monitor shoe
        entering seabed.
    •   Ensure horizontal lines painted every half meter from 2.5 m to 4.0m (top of the LP Housing as the
         starting point). Utilized to verify Conductor land out.
    •   Confirm the LP housing has been painted with a horizontal line at the point of SMO land out.
    •  Two sets of 350T bails (INX2 LL#14) and 250ton shackles can be used to handle the 36” elevators.
    •   Torque RL-4RB connections to 36,000 ftlbs using the belt tongs
    •   Break 1 tab on each joint, 2 tabs on shoe joint
    •   Ensure spare seal kit is available for RL-4RB connections.
    •   Record weights
    •   28” hang off sub to be located 6 joints above the 36” shoe (+/-72m)
    •    Install centralizers as per program.
    •    Fill Conductor with SW while TIH

2)  Pick up (PU) transition joint 36” 552ppf, X-52, RL4-RB, 1.5in wall and the 36” Low Pressure (LP) housing
    c/w extension joint 36” 726ppf, X-52, RL4-RB, 2.0in wall (RL4-RB Pin down) and set support plate in the
    rotary.

    •    Lifting clamps for 36” Housing to be installed onshore
    •  A back-up 36in LP housing is available
    •  Be careful to not damage the ring fitted to the LP Housing (used to provide the lower seal for the
      SMO)
    •  Change to 5” DP elevators.
    •  Add dye to the SW at the top of the conductor (not red as red will be used for cement job).

3)  With the 36” LP housing at rig floor. Install “C” plate (Weatherford) and run 2 joints of fiber glass stinger.

4)  RIH with 2 joints fiberglass stinger and 5” 19.5ppf DP inner string

    •    Drift fiberglass joints before make-up
    •  Space out inner string to leave +/-24m above 36” float shoe.
    •   Paint top single of first stand of the inner string white for reference when pulling out

5) PU CART from the derrick, make-up (M/U) inner string and M/U to LP housing as per Vetco Rep’s
    instructions.

    •   Lock Top Drive
    •   Record String and Running Tool weight
    •   Ensure cement top-up hose does not interfere with CART operation.

6) PU full string to RIH.

    •  Remove “support ring”.
    •    Install Bulls-Eye bracket to the 36” LP Housing (180degrees away from the top-up hose connection)
         in the moon-pool. (Bulls eye reading is 0 – 2 degrees).
    •   Attach soft line to CART valve handle using tie-wrap as a weak point

    •  Take string weight
    •   Record Bulls-Eye inclination reading at surface
    •   Orient conductor the allow bullseye to face rig heading.

7)  Lower the 36” LP housing to sea level

    •  MU Top Drive Sub
    •  Pump seawater through the string with the CART ball valve open to fill drill string and casing.
    •   Close the CART ball valve with a rope in the moon pool.
    •   Circulate sufficiently to confirm no leaks at the RT.
    •  Be prepared to winch rig.
    •  LOCK TOP DRIVE and rotary table to ensure no rotation of the string during running.  Drill crew to
       mark pipe with chalk while RIH check for rotation.

8)  Run conductor on 5” 19.5ppf DP landing string.

    •  ROV to follow 36" conductor to seabed and monitor inclination of bulls eye. Note any significant
       changes in the bullseye reading and record depth.
    •  Pump pad mud down drillstring until visible returns observed by ROV at mudline. Stop pumping and
      RIH without filling pipe.
    •   Record inclination as 36" shoe is stabbed into the hole (ROV to remain close to bullseye and monitor
           all the way to shoe depth denoting any change in angle)
    •     If inclination changes substantially from std to std – the pipe must be worked and possibly circulated
         to reduce angle. This may also include a rig offset.
    •  RIH to place 36” LP housing datum (top) 3.0m above seabed (shoe at +/-660m tvdbrt)
    •  ROV to confirm stickup at mudline
    •  ROV to tap bulls eye to confirm ball movement (Structure pipe inclination must be <1 degree)

9) PU cementing stand with pump in sub and make up to top drive.
    •  Open the compensator
    •  Mark the pipe at rotary level. Monitor the position of this mark to check that the pipe does not move
        during cementing.
    •  ROV to confirm inclination of wellhead less than 1 degree with respect to the readings at the
       moonpool.
    •  ROV to check bullseye and wellhead elevation and request rig floor to adjust elevation accordingly.

      7.1.2.7  Inner String Cementing Operations

1) Do not circulate after reaching TD unless it is pad mud.

    •   Conduct PJSM prior to cementing
    •  Hose cutter / grinder to be installed and tested on ROV
    •  ROV to monitor wellhead during cement job to ensure no flow bypasses running tool.
    •   This will be an inner string job; no landing collar and no plugs.
    •  Cement volumes based on 200% annular excess over gauged hole. Recalculate on rig.

2)  Mix and pump 36” Conductor Cement Slurry with the cement unit as per Cement Program

    •  Pump 50 bbls sea water spacer with RED dye and mica at 6bpm
    •   Pressure test surface lines to 2,000psi.
    •   Mix and pump lead slurry, consisting of 1.50SG “G” Neat cement at 5bpm
         o    If returns of cement are observed with ROV (dye, mica) and minimum 1x annular volume
              (306 bbl) is pumped, stop mixing lead slurry.
    •   Mix and pump tail slurry, consisting of 1.90 SG “G” Neat cement at 4-5 bpm
         o   Last 200bbls of Tail slurry includes CemNET at 2ppb
    •   Displace cement to +/- 12 meters from the shoe with cement unit at 6 bbl/min, slow down to 4
        bbl/min for last 44 bbls as the cement leaves the tailpipe.
    •  Top of Lead slurry planned to be at mudline and Top of tail slurry 50m above shoe.
    •  ROV to Confirm bulls eye reading.

3)  Bleed off and check for backflow

    •     If any back flow, pump back in volume bled and bleed off faster. Repeat three times, if not holding
        close rig floor valve and wait on cement ~4 hrs (confirm based on final tail slurry recipe to be used)
        before dropping top-up ball.

4)  Assuming no back flow, bleed off pressure above TIW valve and drop top-up tool ball

    •   Allow ball to drop, stage up pumps and shear open the sleeve ~800psi
    •  Do not exceed 1,000 psi surface pressure (hose pressure rating) after shearing sleeve.

5) WOC until 300-500 psi compressive strength of tail slurry is reached or until lab tests confirm competent
    cement, before releasing running tool.  Confirm with town prior to releasing tool as current lab tests
    indicate only 360psi compressive strength after 12hrs.

    •  The Darren should be opened after the cement job and circulated very slowly while waiting on
       cement. Circulate seawater at a very low rate (max 150 gpm) through the top up system to prevent
        hole wash out and cement from plugging the system while WOC. ROV should monitor for any crater
       and adjust flow rate down or stop. The chance of the Darren sub failing and inadvertently displacing
       cement is very low.
    •   Wellhead must be stationary while cement sets. ROV to observe.

6)  Perform Top Up Job through top-up system.

    •   Mix and pump a minimum of 80bbls of “G” Neat cement at (1.90SG to match tail slurry)
    •   Displace with sea water at 6 bpm to avoid contaminating top up job.
    •  ROV to record slope indicators and observe seabed around conductor for crater

7)  Release 36” LP Housing Running Tool

    •  ROV to observe wellhead and bulls-eye (inclination should be maximum of 1.0 degree)
    •   Slack off slowly to previously recorded landing string / inner string weight
    •  Back out 36” running tool by using right hand rotation (~5 right hand turns) under Vetco’s instruction
     Shah Deniz D&C                       SDX-5 Operations Drilling Program                       Rev1.04

7.1.3  26” x 32” Hole, 28” Liner (Riserless – RMR contingency) [COND1 changing to LNR1]

7.1.3.1  Section Objectives / TD Criteria

    •    Drill a vertical hole to planned section TD (835m md/tvd brt). Drill to suit 28” Liner tally, BUT do not
          drill deeper than 835m MDBRT / TVDBRT (6m above top of error bar for Q Sand)
    •  Top Set Q Sands
    •   Set 28in Casing at 830m MDBRT /TVDBRT.
    •   Achieve competent cement at the shoe
    •   Isolate potential “fizz gas” zone

7.1.3.2  Hole Section Discussion / Risks / Mitigation

    •   Tight Hole Conditions / Wellbore Stability / Fizz Gas
            1)  According to Shallow Hazards analysis, there is a Low probability of tight hole conditions
                 whilst drilling the Palaeo flow deposits, which occur from 731m +/-12m TVDbrt to 835m +/-
           17m TVDbrt. However, review of SDX-4 drilling experience indicated that hole instability
              problems were encountered in the lower section of the hole which resulted in the need to
            wash down the 28” liner and eventually set it about +/- 3m above planned TD / 28” Landing
              Sub.
            2)  This hole section will be drilled within the potential fizz gas zone. No permeable sands have
             been reported in the SGA within this interval.
            3)  This hole section will be drilled with seawater. The hole section will be drilled underbalanced
            (maximum of about 200 psi). SDX-4 was drilled with a similar underbalance (about 230 psi).
            4)  There is a likelihood to encounter hole instability and fizz gas within this hole section.
            5)  The plan is also to have the mud recovery system (MRS) already rigged up and ready to use
               (1.50sg mud) in case severe hole instability and/or fizz gas conditions are encountered.
            6)  The base plan is to displace the well with a 1.50 sg weighted Pad mud after reaching TD.
            7)  The 28” Liner has a 1000psi pressure seal that will isolate the Fizz Gas.

    •   Shallow Water Flow
            1)  Determined to be Low in Shallow Hazard Analysis
            2)  Possible flow if “Q / Running Sands” are penetrated
            3)  Highest pore pressure is likely at section TD (1.24 sg lower bound “planned” and 1.31 sg
              upper bound “worst case”)
            4) No shallow water flow seen on SDX-4 (Drilled with weighted mud / RMR system – did not
               penetrate Q sands)

    •   Shallow Gas - Determined to be negligible in Shallow Hazard Analysis

    •  Gumbo
            1)  Seawater and Sweeps, successful on INX-1 and INX-2A
            2)  Seawater should disperse gumbo with enough free-water in the system.
            3) RMR rigged up - ability to shift to inhibited mud system at any time.

    •   Failure to lift quality cement to TOL (wash out, formation fracture / losses)
            1)  Use 100% annular excess
            2)  Add CemNET fibers to slurry

7.1.3.3  Planning / Preparations

    •    Drill String: ~830m 5” 19.5ppf, S135
    •   Landing String: ~550m 5” 19.5ppf, S135
    •   Ensure permits are in place for the over the side work planned for this interval.
    •   Close cooperation is required between ROV-Operators, AGR and Driller.  TL Coach to confirm
        robust lines of communication are established and review lines of communication in the pre-job
        meetings. AGR and Oceaneering will require a dedicated radio channel.

    •   While handling BHA or Casing, move the rig off location to avoid damaging the 36” LP Housing on
        the seabed.
    •  A minimum supply of cement and cement additives shall be available on the rig at all times to be
        able to set appropriate isolation plugs.

7.1.3.5  Drilling Operations

1)  Deploy ‘AGR’ Riserless Mud Recovery System (RMR) as per AGR recommended procedures. Confirm
   an adequate weather window exists with all AGR and Oceaneering reps.

    •  The Suction Module (SMO) will be run on drillpipe with lifting sub and landed over the 36” wellhead
       housing
    •  ROV to assist with deployment of seabed pump and hoses and verify landing of SMO
    •  Buoyancy of the RMR hoses is critical (more is better), if not adequate the ROV will bounce on the
       seabed while moving the line from the SMO to the SPM, destroying visibility and costing time.
    •  ROV to connect suction hose to upper section of SMO
    •   Release RT with ROV and pull to surface.
    •   Test SMO control system as per AGR

4)   Drill cement and 36” shoe track.

    •  Tag and Drill Cement (if any) until DTU cutters at the top of cement and pick up of bottom.
    •  Take parameters (up & down weight and free rotation torque).  Ensure the cutters are below any
       mechanical restrictions.
    •   Start rotation (+/- 70 RPM).  Gradually increase flow rate and RPM until desired parameters are
       reached. Start Drilling and Under-reaming (Max weight = 25 klbs, Max RPM = 120)
    •   Allow drum to “creep”. Do not drill-off. Establish a constant rate of penetration and proceed.
    •    Drill cement inside 36” casing to the top of float shoe with seawater w/ 1000gpm, and 50 – 75 RPM.
    •   Viscous pills will be required to remove cement.
    •  Ream shoe track and rathole a minimum of 2 times or until there are no torque spikes.

5)   Drill 26” x 32” hole vertically to section TD (maximum depth of 835m tvdbrt) with lightly viscosified
   Seawater (SW) and viscous sweeps if needed.  [LNR1 once new formation drilled]

    •   Hold  predrill meeting with crew and review “Shallow Gas Procedures”,  “Kill Procedures” and
       “Emergency Move/ Evacuation Procedures”.
    •  ROV to monitor drilling through out for shallow gas using sonar.
    •   Ensure CDC bubble watchers in place. No hot work or non essential personnel on deck while drilling
        surface hole.
    •   Position standby boat upwind/up current prior to spud.
    •  Be aware of “Pumps Off” gas as the fluid in the drillpipe falls. Use PWD to assess whether to pump
      sweeps (system should make its own mud and reduce the number of required hi-vis sweeps).
    •  Pump sweeps if ECD is 0.01 sg above initial drillout readings with SW or indications of hole drag.
    •  Pump 60bbl PHB sweeps every half stand. More frequent if conditions dictate (hole condition,
         flowrate, ROP, returns observed). At connections spot 60 bbl sweep on bottom.
    •   After adding a connection start rotary at slow speed. Apply pump pressure. P/U 2-5m. Bring to
        operating RPM and continue to drill.
    •  Pump at 1150 – 1300 GPM with the rig pumps. Option available to maintain MRS system on slow
      pump rate so majority of fluid will overflow funnel to allow monitoring of mud returns. Only
       implement if required in order to minimize wear to MRS system.
    •   Option to add Xanthan gum (1ppb) to SW system to increase YP and improve carrying capacity.
    •   Maintain rate of penetration (ROP) ~ 10-12m/hr for hole cleaning and to avoid loading up the
       annulus with cutting.
    •     If flow rate is less than 1100gpm, reduce ROP appropriately.
    •  AGR to be on standby to take returns for this interval to provide:
       o  Option to build a weighted SW system with increased fluid loss for increased hole cleaning and
              well bore stability.
       o  Option to monitor MBT trends in SW system by taking returns to the rig
       o  Any hole drag indications – increase Hi-Vis sweeps and consider going to completely closed
            system on AGR and inhibition (consult with office).  Initial MW to be 1.40 SmrsMW SG with the
              option to increase to 1.50 SmrsMW SG if required. Discuss expected changes to ECD,
            standpipe pressure and hole cleaning prior to increasing MW.
    •   Consider nut-plug in sweeps if gumbo is present at mudline
    •   Record the equivalent circulating density (ECD) from the pressure while drilling (PWD) tool for real
        time usage.
    •   Smith DTU Under-reamer operating parameters
        o  Max WOB = 30klbs
        o  Max RPM = 120
        o   Life of cones on DTU = 80hrs at 120 RPM
        o  PSI Range of Cutter Arms = 400 – 800 psi
    •   Try to keep rotary as high as possible to minimize hole angle (taking into account DTU cone life).
    •   Consider pulling to the 36” shoe if hole condition is not good or abnormal over pull is seen.
    •  TD should allow for a 5m rathole beneath the 28” liner shoe – approximately 2m will be 26“ rathole.

            NOTE: On SDX-4 the 28” Liner set circa 3m above landing sub due to hole problems during
                   last 33m of interval.  Not seen as hole  fill issue but more of a wellbore stability problem.
                Reiterates the requirement to ensure hole conditions are adequate prior to running liner.

6)  At TD sweep hole clean with ~200 bbl PHB sweep.

7)  Displace hole with 1.16sg (DHMW @ TD) / 1.50sg Smrs MW WBM

    •   Limit displacement rate to 800 - 900 gpm
    •   Flow Check using subsea camera on SMO.
    •  ROV to observe for shallow gas with sonar. On connections (without DP rotation) call ROV to check
       up close for water or gas flow

8) POOH to 36” casing shoe and flow check for 10minutes.

    •   Pick up a few feet and turn pumps off. Allow 5 minutes rotation before coming out of the hole.
    •   Close AGR Riser valve and flow check using sub sea camera on SMO
    •  Pump mud equal to steel displacement through drillpipe.
    •  Do not back ream with under-reamer.  If hole tight, work through and under-ream down again
    •   Attempt to work through any tight spots first before reaming, ream only if necessary
    •    Driller to ensure hole fill volumes are correct every 3 stands or notify TP or WSL

    •   At the 36” shoe, allow 5 minutes rotation before pulling into the shoe.  Pull into the casing shoe
        slowly.  Ensure hydrostatic head in the  drill string is allowed to equalize before pulling into the
        casing; otherwise, forces of the fluid column may expand cutter arms during entry.
    •   Hole conditions will dictate the need for a wiper trip.   If any doubt let the hole rest and perform a
        wiper trip to TD. On SDX-4 the 28” Liner set circa 3m above landing sub due to hole problems in last
      33m of interval. Not seen as hole fill issue but more of a wellbore stability concern. Reiterates the
       requirement to ensure hole conditions are adequate prior to running liner.

9) POOH to run 28” Liner, racking back the BHA.

    •  Move the rig off location to avoid damaging the 36” LP Housing on the seabed.
    •  Do not delay running 28” liner. Rack back BHA and wait to lay out components that will not be used
         in the next hole section until after running and cementing the liner.
    •  No WL caliper is planned for this interval.

7.1.3.6  Liner Running Operations

1)  Run 28” liner as per tally (28” shoe at +/- 830m TVDBRT / Top of Liner -TOL @ +/-72m above the 36”
    shoe)
    •  Review and update Job Risk Assessments (JRA’s).
    •   Conduct PJSM before running casing.
    •   Rig should be off location (from previous section)
    •  Run Shoe joint (double valves) and check floats hold by buoyancy and by looking down pipe before
           filling.
    •  Make up the RL-4 connections to marks with 28,000ftlbs using Belt Tongs.
    •   Break 1 tab on each joint, 2 tabs on shoe joint.
    •    Install centralizers as per program.
    •    Fill with seawater.

2) PU 28” Casing Hanger Assembly and install C plate (Weatherford) and Bowl (Weatherford) and run 2
     joints fiberglass stinger.
    •   Confirm correct number of 28” RL-4 joints remain on board rig prior to picking up the inner string
    •  Change elevators to 5” DP elevators.
    •   Lock top drive and rotary table to minimise rotation.

3)  RIH with 2 joints fiberglass stinger and 5” DP 19.5ppf inner string.
    •   Paint top single of first stand of the inner string white for reference when pulling out
    •  Space out inner string to leave +/-24m above 28” shoe
    •   Record string weight, for use when backing off the R/T.
    •  ROV to swap AGR return hose to lower port (INX-2A LL#77)

4)  Pick up running tool. M/U inner string to 28” Liner Hanger RT as per Vetco’s instructions. M/U running
     tool to liner.

5) PU full string to RIH.
    •  Run 28” liner on 5” DP landing string.
    •   Attach a rope to the valve handle.
    •  When ball valve of running tool is at the splash zone pump seawater down the inner string (Max 69
       spm) until all air vented from below Wellhead Housing Running Tool (WHHRT). Note: Once running
         tool is below SMO there will not be another opportunity to open/ close the ball valve again to vent
       any trapped air that could be acting on the running tool.
    •   Circulate sufficiently to confirm no leaks
    •  Move the rig over location.
    •   Stop above wellhead and pump pad mud down drillstring until good returns visible at mudline. (do
        not attempt to fill remainder of drillpipe with seawater!)
    •   Utilize ROV to stab 28” Shoe into 36” LP Housing.
    •  Run AGR RMR system to pump displaced mud back to the rig.

6)  RIH and monitor pick up and slack off trends – casing may have to be washed with pad mud to land out
     in hanger profile.

7)  Pick up and make up the cementing stand
    •   Lock rotary. Record up & down weights

8)  Land out 28” Liner for space out with maximum weight ~ 20klbs
    •  Weather sensitive operation – once the 28” snap ring locks it is impossible to perform cement job.
             If there is any chance of inadvertently applying >50klbs then do not attempt to land.
    •  Mark drill pipe for final land out

9) PU 1-2 meters above the 28” landing sub prior to cement job.

7.1.3.7 Cement Operations

1)  While preparing for the cement job, circulate 100 – 200bbls mud at 250gpm.

    •   Rig up surface lines. Cement unit to flush cement line to rig floor and perform a short pressure test
    •   Hold PJSM for cement job while circulating well

2)  Flush AGR RMR and prepare for cementing operations (offline activity) as per AGR recommended
    procedures.

    •   Flush AGR RMR system of WBM – Flush for 10minutes
    •   Ensure that the 6” dumping hose for cement discharge has been installed on the AGR RMR system
    •   Disconnect blind flanges on both sides of the SMO cement return line
    •  Open AGR Diverter valve. Run AGR RMR system at 50%.

3)  Mix & Pump 28” Conductor Liner Cement Slurry with the cement unit as per Cement Program

    •  100% annular excess on Lead and 100% annular excess on Tail (to be recalculated prior to job)
    •   28” liner will be cemented with a 1.55sg Lead and 1.90sg Tail Neat G slurry system at 4-5bpm
       displacement with a 1.50sg SmrsMW. Losses are expected at the end of the job a the open hole
      weak point (1.08sg @ 36” shoe).
    •  Pump 800bbl of MUDPUSH spacer.
    •  Top of Lead is planned for TOL and Top of Tail to 700m (140m above shoe).
    •  CemNET to be used in the last 100bbls of the Lead slurry
    •   Dowell to displace cement at 4-6 bbl/min to leave 12m of cement in shoe track.
    •  Cement unit to bleed off and check for backflow.
    •  TOC to be determined to an appropriate level. As a minimum, volumes pumped and differential
       pressure shall be recorded and reported.
    •  Run the AGR RMR pump for 20 minutes to ensure annulus between 36” conductor and SMO
       adapter is free of cement and to ensure that the cement ports on the 36” conductor are free from
       cement.

4)  Land Out 28” Hanger

    •  Under Vetco’s instruction set 28” seal by RIH the distance picked up and slacking off the full weight
         of the string. Observe shear @ 100klbs.
    •  Take over pull to confirm lock down ~ 50klbs.
    •   Set back cement stand.

5)  Release 28” Running Tool and pull out of hole with inner string

    •   Pull inner string 1 stand out. Circulate 50-100bbl to displace any cement out from inside the inner
         string.
    •   Pull inner string above 28” Liner and circulate out mud to wash any contaminated cement out.
    •   Pull Running Tool to surface and lay out.
    •  ROV to observe inner string paint marking on top of last stand.
    •   Avoid having end of pipe close to wellhead while breaking off stand.

  7.1.4  26” x 28” Hole, 22” Casing (Riserless Mud Recovery) [LNR1 changing to SURF1]

    7.1.4.1  Section Objectives / TD Criteria

  •    Drill a vertical hole to planned section TD (+/-1330m md/tvd brt)
  •   Setting depth based on geo-pick.
  •   Set 22” Casing at +/-1320m md/tvd brt in a competent shale formation (between deep sand-1 and
     deep sand-2).
  •   Achieve cement back to mudline.
  •   Provides sufficient Leak Off to drill subsequent hole section with required mud weight.
  •  No remedial shoe squeeze at 22” shoe.
  •  TD Context / Criteria
           o  Context
                     The shallow seismic has defined a ~80-m shale sequence bounded by two thin
                       sands (referred to as “deep sand-1” and “deep sand-2”). There is a +/-28m
                             error bar for deep sand-1 and a +/-31m error bar for deep sand-2. The error
                         bar for the thickness of the 80-m shale is +/-13m.
                          Opportunity to deepen the 22” shoe setting depth to increase the narrow drilling
                      window for the next interval. Small margin between MW and FG at the 22”
                         shoe.  Required to  drill with 1.48sg DHMW while the predicted FG is only
                         1.521sg.  If set deeper, the predicted FG could increase to 1.549sg.
                     Shoe depth limitation based on string weight and requirement to avoid setting
                      shoe in sands.
           o   Criteria
                                           If base of deep sand-1 is On Depth or Deeper, drill to 50m below deep sand-1.
                     The base of deep sand-1 is prognosed @ 1280m TVDBRT +/-28m.
                                           If base of deep sand-1 is Shallow, drill to 30m below the deep sand-2 (base of
                      deep sand-2 is prognosed @ 1382m TVDBRT +/-31m).
                                           If deep sand-1 can not be identified, drill to 1350m TVDBRT.   If sand seen at
                    1350m TVDBRT, consult with town prior to drilling ahead.
                     The actual pick and casing setting depth must be refined using real time LWD
                           log data. NOTE: the MWD tool will also be equipped with GR cartridge in the
                         event of LWD tool failure

    7.1.4.2  Hole Section Discussion / Risks / Mitigations

•   Tight Hole Conditions / Shallow Water Flow / Wellbore Stability
      o    According to the SGA document, there is a Low probability of tight hole conditions whilst
                  drilling the Palaeo flow deposits, which occur over several intervals within this section.
             Notable intervals are:
                835m +/-17m TVDbrt to 857m +/-18m
                963m +/-23m TVDbrt to 983m +/-24m
                1027m +/-26m TVDbrt to 1089m +/-30m
                1169m +/-34m TVDbrt to 1221m +/-36m
      o    This hole section will be drilled through the Q-sands and Apsheron intervals.
      o    The Q-sands interval will be drilled underbalanced.
      o    Flows from the Q-sands intervals were observed in the SDX-2 and SDX-3 wells when drilled
             underbalanced. Also, drilling experience in SDX-4 indicated that high gas readings as well
            as water cut mud were detected within this interval.
                 SDX-4 (riserless w/AGR): Drilled the section underbalanced. No Flows were
                     reported within Q-sands but drilling observation suggested that hole section was
                          drilled under-balance which agrees with model estimate.
                 SDX-3 (riser installed): Flows were reported within Q-sands. Required to increase
           MW to kill the flow.
      o    There is a high potential of flows, high gas readings or bubbles and hole instability while
                  drilling the Q-sands section in SDX-05 (840m to 950m TVDbrt).

[ صفحه 54 از 160 ]
────────────────────────────────────────────
      o    This hole section will be drilled using a dual gradient (MRS) with a mud weight of 1.50 sg. If
             hole instability and/or high gas readings are observed, then there is an option to increase the
                  drilling mud from 1.50sg to 1.60sg.
      o    The well will be displaced with a 1.75 sg weighted Pad mud after reaching TD.
      o    Highest pore pressure is not likely at section TD, but rather at the Q-sands (1.26 sg lower
           bound “planned” at the Q-sands).
      o    This section may have to be drilled and cemented quickly as most operations (drilling/pad-
            mud/cementing) may have to be performed in under-balance conditions.

•   Shallow Gas
      o    Small amplitude anomaly is present at 1452m TVDBRT (+/-47m). Based on current plan,
              this anomaly will not be penetrated in this interval. The risk of encountering a shallow
            gas accumulation in this anomaly is considered to be Low.

•   Stuck Pipe
      o    Sweeps to clean the hole as required while drilling
      o    Enlarge well bore using 28in under-reamer
      o    Option to make a dedicated wiper trip with stiff assembly to mimic casing
      o     Limit set down weight with casing to 50 Klbs above PU / SO weights prior to entering 26in
             hole with casing.

•  AGR System Failure
      o     In the event the AGR system fails, the contingency plan will involve drilling with SW &
           Sweeps and reverting to pump & dump as required (limited WBM capacity in the mud pits).

•  AGR Return Hose Failure
      o    The use of 1.75 sg mud approaches the limits of the return hose design. Desired safety
               factor = 1.5, but with the 1.75 sg fluid in the hoses the SF at the Hose Handling Platform =
             1.46 and the SF at the lowest buoyancy module (380m ABOVE ML) = 1.33. NOTE – the
           weak link in the system is the hose coupling.
      o   No personnel to work on the hose handling platform with 1.75 sg WBM in the return system.
             Return hose must be flushed with SW first.

•   Hole Enlargement – Risk to Cement Job
      o   Run 22in Casing into 26in rat hole at TD
      o     Utilizing AGR and inhibited mud to minimize washout.

•   Failure to lift quality cement to mudline (wash out, formation fracture / losses)
      o    Use 100% annular excess on slurries
      o    Add CemNET fibers to slurry

•   Flow After Cementing
      o    Once cement is in place, the predicted pressure of the Q sands will be at balance with the
              hydrostatic of the cement column (both at 1.26SG). NOTE: this assumes the lower bound
             pressure profile (refer to Shallow PP Profile in Section 4)
      o    As the cement transitions from liquid to solid, there is the opportunity for the well to flow
            (assuming the Q sands are mobile).
      o    Review procedures for holding back pressure on the 36” x 22” annulus with the AGR system
                 until the lead slurry sets.
      o        If required, take measures to ensure SMO is not cemented to the 36” LP Housing

    7.1.4.3  Planning / Preparations

  •    Drill String: ~1300m 5” 19.5ppf, S135
  •   Landing String: ~550m 5” 34ppf, S135
  •   Ensure special drift available (2.935”)
  •   Ensure permits are in place for the over the side work planned for this interval.
  •   Close cooperation is required between ROV-Operators, AGR and Driller.  TL Coach to confirm
      robust lines of communication are established and review lines of communication in the pre-job
      meetings. AGR and Oceaneering will require a dedicated radio channel.

10) Drill 28” window with DTU tool.

    •  Lower the tool into the hole until it reaches the top of the section to be enlarged
    •   Distance between DTU arms (in open position) and the Bit is 25m – To Be Confirmed by Smith
        Supervisor at the Rig.
    •  RIH till 17000 DTU arms are 5m below the shoe.
    •  Take parameters (up & down weight and free rotation torque).
    •   Start rotation (+/- 70 RPM).
    •   Gradually increase flow rate and RPM until desired parameters are reached. Underream 3-5m
        leaving bit at least 5m off TD. Shut down rotation, slowly pick up 1-2 meters and slack of to perform
       a shoulder test (5-10 klbs) to confirm arms are open.
    •   Cutter arms should be fully open now. Considering the shallow formation, option to repeat the above
        steps. The second time, there should be no weight, and should start taking weight when reach the
        shoulder is tagged.
    •   Increase RPM to 80-100 maximum.
    •   Allow drum to “creep”. Do not drill-off.
    •   Establish a constant rate of penetration and proceed.

11) Drill 26” x 28” hole vertically to section TD (+/-1330m MD / TVDbrt) with a 1.50sg (SmrsMW) / 1.29sg
   (EDHMW @ TD) water based Mud.

    •   During  first BU, Mud Engineer to check mud properties for indication of water seeping into the
        wellbore from the formation (Q-sand exposed during BHA trip).
    •   Hold  predrill meeting  with crew and review  Kill Procedures, Emergency Move  / Evacuation
       Procedures and Shallow Gas Procedures.
    •   Ensure CDC bubble watchers in place. No hot work or non essential personnel on deck while drilling
        surface hole.
    •   Position standby boat upwind/up current.
    •  Be aware of “Pumps Off” gas as the fluid in the drillpipe falls
    •   Flow check by closing AGR Riser valve and monitoring SMO funnel with AGR sub sea camera to
       determine static losses or flow.
    •   Trip sheets shall be filled out by the driller on every trip in and out of the hole.
    •   Record the equivalent circulating density (ECD) from the pressure while drilling (PWD) tool for real
        time usage.
    •   Try to keep rotary as high as possible to minimise hole angle.
    •   Control WOB as required to maintain verticality.
    •   Control ROP drilling into the “Q Sands”. Drill interval with caution and confirm BHA is always free
       having stopped the pumps and prior to connections.
    •   Smith DTU Under-reamer operating parameters
        o  Max WOB = 30klbs
        o  Max RPM = 100
        o   Life of cones on DTU = 80hrs at 120 RPM
        o  PSI Range of Cutter Arms = 400 – 800 psi
    •   After adding a connection start rotary at slow speed.  Apply pump pressure. P/U 2- 5m.  Bring to
        operating RPM and continue to drill.
    •   Monitor mud parameters carefully while drilling “Q Sands” as there have been Brine flows on other
        wells and the exact pore pressure is not known with certainty
    •   Option available to increase to a 1.60sg (SmrsMW) / 1.34sg (EDHMW @ TD) water based Mud
    •     If fluid level in the SMO funnel rises and returns overflow into the open sea, immediately back off on
          rig pumps to 400gpm and pick up off bottom as far as possible. Work the pipe up and down with low
      rpm (20 – 30 rpm) to avoid getting stuck while investigating and solving the problem.
    •     If any problems occur with the pumps,  if at all possible, do not stop pumping. Maintain circulation
       (>400gpm) to prevent cuttings from settling out on the top of the BHA. Keep pipe moving while
         circulating to avoid washouts in one location.
    •  TD should allow for a 10m rathole beneath the 22” casing shoe. This is enough rat hole to account
         for any  fill on bottom and still be able to land the HP Housing in the LP Housing on top of the 36”
        conductor.
    •  ROV to observe for shallow gas with sonar. On connections (without DP rotation) call ROV to check
       up close for water or gas flow.

    •   Section can be drilled at 15 – 20 m/hr ROP with a 1.50sg SmrsMW (1.29sg EMW Gradient @ TD),
       1100 – 1200 gpm and FAIR - GOOD hole cleaning. The ECD at the shoe (1.167SG) is below the
      minimum open hole fracture strength (1.28sg @ 28” shoe).   If MW is increased to 1.60 sg, consult
       with town to verify updated drilling parameters prior to drilling ahead.

[ صفحه 67 از 160 ]

13) Place a 1.9SG pill in the bottom 10m of rat-hole to prevent cement from slumping.

14) Displace hole with 1.43sg (EDHMW) / 1.75sg SmrsMW WBM (Cl diluted <21,000ppm)
        •  NOTE: prior to weighting up the pad mud and displacing, have a conversation with town to
            confirm the required density of the pad mud (depends on flowcheck results and hole condition
            while drilling the section).
        •   Flow Check using subsea camera on SMO.
        •  Manage pressure and ECD accordingly while displacing the heavy pad mud.  Virtual Hydraulics
            calculations indicate ability to pump at 1050 gpm and keep ECD under the weak point (28” shoe)
        •   1.75 sg WBM is approaching the working limit of the return hose clamps at this water depth. Be
           prepared to react accordingly if return hose fails.

15) POOH to 28” liner shoe and flow check for 10 minutes.
    •   Pick up a few feet and turn pumps off. Allow 5 minutes rotation before coming out of the hole.
    •   Close AGR Riser valve and flow check using sub sea camera on SMO
    •  Swab / Surge (MI’s Virtual Hydraulics) calculation to be performed prior to POOH to determine max
         pulling speeds.
    •   Slow trip speed when pulling through “Q Sands” to prevent swabbing in sand.
    •  Pump mud equal to steel displacement through drill pipe
    •   Attempt to work through any tight spots first before reaming, ream only if necessary
    •    Driller to ensure hole fill volumes are correct every 3 stands or notify TP or WSL
    •   At the 28” shoe, allow 5 minutes rotation before pulling into the shoe.  Pull into the casing shoe
        slowly.  Ensure hydrostatic head in the  drill string is allowed to equalize before pulling into the
        casing; otherwise, forces of the fluid column may expand cutter arms during entry.
    •   Hole conditions will dictate the need for a wiper trip.   If any doubt let the hole rest and perform a
        wiper trip to TD (don’t want to stick 22” off bottom).

16) Continue POOH to run 22” surface casing, rack back the BHA.

    •  When bit is at SMO, displace string to SW prior to POOH.
    •     If indications of hole problems exist, option to run a wiper trip BHA with 4x 26in stabilizers to mimic
        22” casing stiffness. Team to be aware that spiral stabilizers will have more tendency to pack off.
    •  Do not delay running surface casing. Rack back BHA and wait to lay out components that will not be
       used in the next hole section until after running the casing. The 9.5” Drill Collars and 9” Anadrill
      (PWD/Power pulse) tools are planned for drilling the next 17-1/2” x 22” open-hole section.
    •  Move the rig off location to avoid damaging the 36” LP Housing on the seabed.
    •  No WL caliper is planned for this interval.

      7.1.4.6  22” Surface Casing Running Operations       [SURF]

1)  Run 22” casing as per tally with shoe at +/- 1320m TVDBRT.

    •   Vetco Running tool capacity (700K lbs tension including 100K overpull) is exceeded with 22” casing
        run past 1,480m MDbrt.
    •   Ensure Vetco H4 High Capacity clamp is in use.
    •  Due to the weight of the 22” casing string and operating at the upper end of the limits of the handling
             / running equipment, it is highly unlikely that pulling the 22” will be an option, should there be issues
        while running.
    •  Review and update JRA’s.
    •   Conduct PJSM before running casing
    •   Ensure 18 ¾” CART is racked back in derrick
    •   Confirm shoe track is locked with all 4 x RL-4S anti-rotation tabs.
    •  M/U RL-4S 22''x 1''connections to 45,000 ft-lbs and break one anti-rotation tab.
    •   Ensure seal kit for RL-4S connections is available.
    •  Check floats hold by buoyancy and by looking down pipe.
    •    Fill the pipe with mud, enough to balance SW while running to the wellhead (work out U-tube
       schedule)
    •    Fill 22” casing and DP with low chlorides (<21000ppm) 1.75sg (SmrsMW) water based Pad mud.
    •    Install Vetco 18” Liner Hanger sub 100m above the 22” shoe.
    •    Install Vetco 16” Liner Hanger sub 200m above the 22” shoe.
    •   Stop at LPH and refill casing again until good returns at mudline of WBM.
         o  Stop again at 28-in shoe depth and refill casing until mud returns at seafloor – document
             volume to fill pipe.
    •  Mark DP with paint for landing out HP housing with SMO engaged (unable to visually observe the
     HP Housing land out due to SMO interference).
    •   Paint a horizontal line on the HP housing to verify land out.
    •   Lock top drive and rotary table to minimise rotation
    •   Continue to take returns to surface via AGR RMR while running casing
    •    Install centralizers as per program.  Place centralizer towards the lower end of the joints on shoe
         track.
    •  ROV to follow 22" casing to monitor stab-in into the LPH.

2) PU 10ft burst disc sub and crossover joint (pre-made in town)

    •  Do not set slips on the Burst Disc
    •  Do not use Belt Tong over Burst Disc
    •   Visually confirm disc is intact
    •  BP WSL to witness M/U and running
    •   Confirm casing is completely free to move up and down before setting slips.
    •   Note string weight

3)  Change to 500T 5” Drill pipe elevators

    •  The 5” 34ppf Landing String is required to run this casing string, driven by slip crushing loads.

4) PU 18 ¾” HP Housing assembly and install C Plate (Vetco) and bowl (Weatherford).

    •  Check correct number of 22” X60 RL-4S joints remain onboard rig prior to picking up inner string.
    •   Record casing string weight
    •  Review hole condition, rig heave and string weight before hanging casing off on clamp.
    •  H4 Clamp with Split housing (High Capacity) is rated to 1,000 kips.

5)  RIH 2 joints fiberglass stinger and 5” 19.5lb/ft drillpipe inner string

    •   Paint top single of first stand of the inner string white for reference when pulling out

    •  Space out inner string to leave +36m above the 22” shoe
    •   Ensure tailpipe of inner string is below 18” hanger profile.
    •   Record string weight, for use when backing off the RT.
    •  ROV to swap AGR return hose to lower port (INX-2A LL#77)

6) PU RT, M/U inner string and HP wellhead to 18 ¾” HP Wellhead Assembly RT as per Vetco’s
    instruction.

    •   Place dye in the casing prior to M/U the Running Tool.
    •   Vetco to remove blank and insert ball valve in the running tool and ensure it is open.

7) PU full string and RIH

    •   Continue to  fill 22” casing and DP with low chlorides (<21000ppf) 1.50sg (SmrsMW)  / 1.29sg
     (EDHMW @ TD) water based mud.
    •   Note and Record casing/drill pipe weights when PU casing.
    •  Remove Vetco H4 High Capacity clamp w/ Split Housing
    •   Pull Master bushing
    •  AGR MRS system will need to be running to take displaced mud back to surface
    •  RIH until wellhead is at working height in moon pool area. Double check 2” ball valve on CART is
       open.
    •   Ensure correct orientation of ball valve handle to be able to close without clashing.
    •   Attach a rope to the ball valve handle, using a tie wrap as weak point.
    •  When ball valve of running tool is at the splash zone, pump mud down the inner string using mud
      pumps until all air vented from below WHRT.
    •   Close ball valve using the rope and continue pumping to confirm that the ball valve is closed and no
        leaks around the running tool.

    •  NOTE: Once running tool is below SMO there will not be another opportunity to open the ball valve
       again to vent any trapped air that could be acting on the running tool.

    •     If wellhead full, continue running in hole. Vetco rep onsite to confirm.
    •  ROV to observe APB sub immediately above 36” housing. Stop here and circulate / fill pipe
       with 100 bbls of WBM while the ROV closely inspects the burst disk for fluid leaking.
    •    Install top drive and break circulation to verify there is no leak through the APB sub. BP WSL to
        witness.
    •  ROV to follow HPWH Housing to ML and monitor inclination of bulls eye. Note any significant
       changes in the bullseye reading and record depth.
    •    Fill drill pipe with mud prior to making up cement stand. (Note – Lesson Learned #7 A02: Circulate
      down last 50m to bottom reduced standpipe pressure from 240 to 60 psi and reduce packing off. If
       any resistance, commence pumping while working the pipe.)
    •  Max set down while running 22” = 50klbs
    •  Take good PU and SO weights prior to entering 26” rat hole.
    •  Wash string down 26” rat hole and monitor closely for hole drag and pack off tendency.

8) PU and M/U the cementing stand

    •   Ensure rotary is locked
    •   Record up and down weights and land 22” surface casing.

9)  Land out HP housing and slack off 150K to ensure wellhead is fully landed out. Take ~ 50klbs overpull
    over 22” string weight for assurance that wellhead is fully landed in 36” housing.

    •   Unable to visually observe wellhead land out due to SMO interference
    •  Once 22” casing has been confirmed to be locked in, return to neutral weight for cement job. Once
      Cement job is complete full string weight is slacked off to release R/T.
    •   Hold Casing weight until after cementing
    •   Slacking off the casing weight energises the 18 ¾” HP housing to the 36” LP Housing

      7.1.4.7  Cementing Operations    [SURF]

1)  While preparing for cement job,

    •   Circulate the hole at cementing displacement rates for the inner string and 36m of 22-in casing to
       ensure no restrictions.
    •  Pump the cement job immediately after conditioning.
    •   Line up cement unit to avoid circulating large volumes of mud.
    •   Rig up cement lines. Cement unit to flush line to rig floor and pressure test.
    •   Rig pumps to pump 100bbls spacer with red dye and mica at 6bpm.
    •   Rig floor to apply ~500psi behind closed IBOP

2)  Flush AGR RMR and prepare for cementing operations (offline activity) as per AGR recommended
    procedures

    •   Flush AGR RMR system of WBM – at least 10 minutes
    •  The ROV will have to line out the AGR SMO and SPM to dilute wellhead returns with seawater prior
         to cementing the 22” casing.
         o  Disconnect blind flanges on both sides of the SMO cement return line
         o  Move suction hose from Mud Return system to cement system
         o  Open AGR Diverter valve
         o  Ensure that the 6” dumping hose for cement discharge has been installed on the AGR RMR
              system
    •  Run AGR RMR system diluting returns at the mudline to maintain <21,000ppm chlorides content
        during the cement job. (No returns will be taken to the rig during the cement job.)

3)  Mix & Pump 22” Surface Casing Cement Slurry as per Cement Program.
    •  Cemcade Hydraulics: 22” surface casing will be cemented with a 1.77sg Lead and 1.90sg Tail Neat
     G slurry system at 4-5bpm displacement with a 1.75sg SmrsMW. Losses are predicted at the end of
       displacement at 22” shoe (assumes the conservative lower bound FG of 1.46sg @ 22” shoe).
    •  Top Lead planned at seabed and Top of Tail 100m above 22” Shoe.
    •  Volumes based on100% annular excess over gauged hole (recalculate prior to job)
    •  Pump 100bbls of MUDPUSH spacer with red dye and mica at 6bpm with rig pumps.
    •   Mix and pump LEAD slurry of class “G” Neat cement at 1.77 SG with cement unit.
         o    If ROV observes cement returns (red dye, mica), and minimum 1x annular volume (850 bbl)
                    is pumped, stop mixing Lead slurry and mix/pump Tail slurry.
    •   Mix and pump TAIL slurry, class “G” Neat cement at 1.90 SG.
         o   Last 200bbls of Tail slurry to include CemNET at 2ppb
    •   Displace cement to place Top of Lead at mudline and Top of Tail cement 100m above the 22” shoe.
    •  Cement to be displaced to 24m above the shoe inside 22” casing.
    •  ROV to notify cement unit that red dye has been seen and to notify BP WSL.
    •  Cement unit to bleed off and check for backflow.
    •  TOC to be determined to an appropriate level. As a minimum, volumes pumped and differential
       pressure shall be recorded and reported.
    •  Leave the AGR RMR System running for 20 minutes to ensure annulus between 36” conductor and
     SMO adapter is free of cement and to ensure that the cement ports on the 36” conductor are free of
       cement.
    •     If deemed feasible, without adding additional risk, utilize the AGR system to hold back pressure on
        the 36” x 22” annulus until the lead slurry sets. NOTE: at the point of program issue, this option was
             still being reviewed by the engineering & operational team.

4)  Release 18 ¾” RT and POOH with inner string

    •   With neutral weight of the inner and landing string at the wellhead, rotate 5 turns to the right to
        release running tool.

     Shah Deniz D&C                       SDX-5 Operations Drilling Program                       Rev1.04

    •   Note string weight

5)  Set Back Cement Stand

    •   Insert wiper dart and pump through string at 5bpm using seawater
    •   Alternative option to pump scour pill

6)  Pull 18 ¾” RT to surface and lay out inner string.

    •  ROV to observe white joint of drillpipe pulled out of 18 ¾” housing for space configuration.
    •  ROV to observe inner string paint marking on top of last stand.
    •   Avoid having end of pipe close to wellhead while breaking off stand.
    •   Lay out fiberglass joints.

7)  Retrieve ‘AGR’ Riserless Mud Recovery System (RMR).

    •   Maximize offline activity
    •  The Suction Module (SMO) will be retrieved on drillpipe
    •  ROV to assist with recovery of seabed pump module (SPM) and hoses.
    •  ROV to perform a wellhead VX-VT profile survey with BP WSL to confirm bullseye reading.

8)  Have ROV perform survey around wellhead for signs of cratering.  Determine the need for top up job
    (craters on SDX-4 and INX-2 were similar in appearance but INX-2 required top-up job stinger). If crater
    radius exceeds 1m from conductor OD, contingency plan is to run into crater / 36" annulus with 3-1/2”
   DP and completely fill annulus with cement.

9) RUN 18 ¾” 15k BOP STACK & RISER. The BOP/Wellhead will already have been stump tested to
    10,000psi except for the Annulars which will have been tested to 7000psi (70% of 10K psi rating).
   [SURF]

    •  C&K lines to be tested once at the start of Riser running and once at the end.
    •  Run BOP Isolation Test Tool (BOPITT) to test BOP connector to 10K psi (limited by 10K psi C&K
         lines on the riser on loan from DDGG).
    •  BOP stump test will serve as primary BOP test. Only required to perform function test once landed.
    •   Refer to: GSF Istiglal – Riser Analysis - SDX-5 Caspian Sea, February 12th 2008 for proposed Riser
       Stackup, tension analysis and tensioner recommendations.
