7.1.5 17 ½” x 22” Hole, 18” Intermediate Liner  [SURF1 changing to LNR2]

  7.1.5.1  Section Objectives / TD Criteria

•   18” Liner planned setting depth of +/-2,586m MD / TVDbrt is based on pore pressure and allowable
     drilling window.
•   Set in Upper Surakhany mudstone, above the predicted Surakhany pressure ramp. The actual pick
   and casing setting depth will be refined using real time LWD log data due to the error bar at this
    depth.
•   Provide sufficient kick tolerance to drill the next section.
•  TD Criteria:
        1)   Drill to a maximum depth to ensure that the 2nd Surakhany anhydrite is NOT penetrated, i.e.
            set 18” liner above the Surakhany pressure ramp. The TD of the 22” hole section will be
           Geo-Picked.
        2)  Primary Plan: The interval between 1st and 2nd Anhydrite is expected to be approximately
        80m TVD / 80m MD, giving a Top 1st Anhydrite at +/-2570m TVDBRT / MDBRT. Drill to 50m
       MD below Top 1st Anhydrite, this will allow the 18” shoe to be set 16m TVD below the Top 1st
            Anhydrite (29m MD pilot hole and 5m MD rat hole).
        3)  Backup Plan ‘Topdown Approach’: If after drilling 160m below the top of the Surakhany
              (identified by LWD), the first Surakhany Anhydrite has not been seen, stop drilling and set
           18” liner (all offset wells on Shah Deniz have thicknesses of c.129 -143m from top
          Surakhany to the first anhydrite).
•  Cement lifted to TOL

  7.1.5.2  Hole Section Discussion / Risks / Mitigations

•   Faults
         o  The “Shallow Fault” is expected at +/-1923m TVDbrt (+/-250m).
         o  No other wells drilled to date in Shah Deniz have encountered any significant faults in
                the overburden section, thus limiting the ability to quantify the risk associated. Rigsite
             needs to be monitoring and prepared to react to potential problems associated
              with fault (torque, stuck pipe, losses, etc.).
         o  The first fault (commonly called the shallow fault) expected to be encountered will be in
             a package containing a strong field wide reflector. This occurs near the tip out point of
                the fault where the throw is decreasing but should still see at least 40m of throw. In the
            SDX-4 well, this seismic facies was associated with low net to gross, mostly silts and
               shales with occasional sand.
         o   Drilling through the shallow fault with the planned mudweight of 1.48SG is unlikely to
              cause losses, unless the ECD is significantly higher than the planned DHMW. The risk
                 of lost circulation increases if the fault is penetrated shallower than planned. This risk
              decreases with depth.
         o   Lost Circulation Material is an option to prevent losses, but lowering ECD may be
               another solution. However, during discussions to reduce MW, it need to be clear that
               reducing mudweight can enhance wellbore failure by breakout.
         o  The breakout analyses demonstrate that the planned mudweight of 1.48SG will result in
            some compressive failure through the fault zones. The breakout severity decreases if
                the faults are encountered shallow rather than deeper in the subsurface.
         o  The wellbore azimuth is oriented in the direction of SHmax, therefore breakout will occur
                   in the sides of the hole, which should be less problematic for hole cleaning
         o  Managing the drilling risks through this fault interval will require balancing downhole
             mudweight to limit the risk of losses (which requires lower mudweight), yet keeping
             mudweight high enough to reduce breakout. Optimising hole cleaning procedures and
               monitoring cuttings volumes will be key as it will be unlikely that zero breakout can be
              achieved (high MW required) without risking losses at the casing shoe or into the fault
               zone.

•   Tight Drilling Window

         o  Small margin between MW and FG at the 22” shoe. Required to drill with 1.48sg DHMW
                while the predicted FG is only 1.521sg (assuming shoe set at 1320m TVDBRT).
         o   Historical offsets indicate LOT / FIT has been higher than the predicted FG (assuming
              competent cement jog at the 22” shoe).
         o  Heightened awareness required for the management of mud properties, ECD, and Swab
           & Surge.

•    Well Control
         o   Limited Kick Tolerance (6bbls) for this interval due to the limited FG at 22” Shoe. Will
                require increased awareness prior to and during the drilling of this interval.
                      During the pre-section meeting and prior to drilling the hole section the well
                         control issues will be emphasized and discussed with the offshore drilling team.
                     Heightened awareness of the entire drilling team will be maintained during the
                       hole section. Drills to be carried out to confirm this.
                     Requirement for tight pit management to avoid false gains. The Derrickman or
                 Mud Engineer must inform the Driller and the Mudloggers prior to any mud
                       treatment or transferring operations taking place. The pit volume totalizer should
                    be utilized and the alarms set and functional.
                   The importance of early kick detection will be stressed to the rig crew and
                     Mudloggers at all safety and pre-shift meetings.
                             All rig and Mudloggers kick detection equipment will be fully functional prior to
                       the start of the section and the alarms will be set on pits and flow back +/- 2bbls
                         active and 2% flow on rig sensors, and +/-2bbls pit and 5% flow on Geoservices.
                      Ensuring that the hole is clean and the mud is within specification prior to
                       running casing.

•   Shallow Gas
         o  Small amplitude anomaly will be intersected at 1452m TVDBRT (+/-47m). The risk of
               encountering a shallow gas accumulation in this interval is considered to be Low.

•   Pore Pressure Ramp
         o  The first anticipated pressure ramp occurs between the first and second Surakhany
                anhydrite (between Top Surakhany and the se220 pick). The pressures are predicted to
               increase from 1.4 sg to 1.6 sg. Note: This ramp actually starts higher and is more
               gradual than what is shown on the PP/FG plot where the ramp is abrupt and starts at the
             se220 pick. The projected SDX-4 MDT pressure point at 2621m TVDBRT (1.46 sg)
                 highlights this.
         o   This hole section is not expecting to penetrate this higher pressured sand (located below
                the 2nd anhydrite) but vigilant monitoring must be adhered to while drilling this interval.
               Refer to TD Criteria above.
         o  Weight-up the 1.41sg SMW /1.43sg DHMW starting density to 1.46sg SMW /1.48sg
         DHMW by 1600m MDbrt (prior to reaching the top error bar of the first overburden fault).
               This provides some relief if the ELOT is lower than expected.

•   Lost Circulation
         o  Down hole losses may be induced while drilling and running & cementing casing. The
              “Shah Deniz SDX-5 Lost Circulation Strategy” will be available for reference.
         o  Risk of lost circulation is elevated due to drilling through the Shallow Fault.
         o   Drilling Fluid will be treated with LPM.
         o  Surge calculations to determine acceptable running speeds to minimize chances of
               losses

•   Wellbore Stability
         o MW for this interval will be above or equivalent to the recommended MW for the
                predicted WBS line for most of the interval. The MW will transition to a level below the
                predicted WBS mud weight at the base of the section to be drilled.
         o   Monitor cuttings returns for indication of wellbore instability.
         o   Monitor for torque and drag towards the lower interval of the hole section.
         o   Possible option to increase the MW. This must be discussed and agreed with town prior
                  to taking action. Increasing the MW increases risks such as losses at the previous shoe

         o   This interval will contain a long rathole (17-1/2” pilot hole) which will provide additional
              space for hole fill generated by wellbore instability.

  7.1.5.3  Planning / Preparations

•    Drill String: ~2600m 6-5/8in 27.7ppf S135. Ensure enough 6 5/8” drillpipe (DP) has been picked up
    to drill to TD. 120 stands of 6 5/8” DP can be racked back. Plan forward is to maximize the usage of
   6 5/8” DP to TD largely driven by improved hydraulics.
•   Landing String: ~1300m 5” 34ppf S135
•   Rigsite Supervisors to review monitoring and first response procedures for potential
   problems associated with fault drilling (torque, stuck pipe, losses, etc) with rig crews. NOTE:
   Engineering Team to provide short presentation on fault drilling practices prior to drilling this
    hole section.
•   Fluids Engineer to prepare fluid  / pit management plan prior to the start of the hole section. The
    water in the riser and 1.75 sg WBM will be swapped to 1.43 sg DHMW LTOBM prior to drilling out
    the shoe track. May require a Class A vessel on location to assist with fluid management.
•  Mud pumps to be dressed with 7” Liners
•   Slip crushing calculations drive the use of 34# landing string. The load at the top of the landing
    string with 100Klbf overpull is 558klbs.
•   Measure, tally and internal drift the 18” liner and float shoe to 16.50”.
•   Caliper ID of 10% of casing joints for use in cement displacement calculations (onshore inspection
    services to provide multi-armed caliper information for accuracy in displacement calculations).
•   External drift the 18” liner and centralizer subs to 18.20”. The Liner must pass the 18.22” restriction
     in the 22” Landing Joint w/ 18" Sub.
•   18” Bow spring centralizer subs will be installed on the pin end of the joints onshore.
•  The primary shoe track will be MU on shore.
•  The liner will be run and cemented using the SSR (Sub-Sea Release) plug system requiring a Baker
    (3 dart) cement head. Note: Baker to supply XOs.
      o  XO (6-5/8” FH box up x 6-5/8” Reg pin down)
      o  Baker (3 dart) cement head (6-5/8” Reg Box up / Pin down) loaded with the following:
                  Vetco 2.9” hanger “dart” (confirm shear discs are 4,500psi) in the upper chamber
                  Weatherford top cement drillpipe dart in middle chamber
                  Weatherford bottom cement drillpipe dart in the lower chamber
      o  XO (6-5/8” Reg box up x 5” NC50 pin down) Special Drift required – drift with Vetco dart

[ صفحه 85 از 160 ]
────────────────────────────────────────────
    •   This assembly will have a dual Rhino Reamer (RR) configuration. The Upper RR will be a 19-1/2in
       Cleanout RR  / Stabilizer and the bottom RR will open to 22in. The Cleanout RR / Stabilizer has
        modified cutting pads for drilling the shoe track and will act as stabilization above the primary RR.
    •   Test both Rhino Reamers (RR) at surface as per Smith rep.
         o  The Lower 22” RR will be ball drop activated and will be pinned (in close position). Gauge
              Rhino Reamer at surface.
         o  Ensure the Cleanout RR opens, and fully retracts to collapsed diameter. This Rhino will be
               run without ball drop system, and will therefore be unpinned. Gauge Cleanout Rhino at
                surface. WSL to witness.
    •   Slack off until the Cleanout Rhino Reamer cutters are below the rotary table. Bring the mud pumps
        online and gradually increase the flow rate to the pre-established value as specified in the hydraulic
        analysis for the drill out. Verify that the cutters HAVE BEEN ACTIVATED.
    •  Take care when running through the BOP, wellhead, and 16in and 18in Hang-off subs (~200m and
      ~100m above the 22” shoe respectively).
    •  Minimum ID of 17.61” at the 18-3/4” NSP. Next restriction is 18.22” at the 18in Hang-off Sub.
    •   Perform Well Control Drills (note that drill ahead fluid will not be in the hole yet).

2)  Displace wellbore, riser, and choke & kill lines to 1.41sg SMW  / 1.43sg DHMW LTOBM as per mud
    engineer’s procedures.

    •   Surface mud weights (SMW) are estimates, operational decisions will be based on Down Hole Mud
       Weights (DHMW).
    •   Displacement will require recovering as much of the UltraDril WBM as possible for return to mud
         plant. MI will have a detailed written plan in place for swapping to LTOBM and recovering the Water
      Based Mud.   The MI  should  include  Pit management, and  proper  discharge  of  returning
      seawater/WBM overboard.
    •   Plan to weight-up the 1.41sg SMW/ 1.43sg DHMW starting density to 1.46sg SMW/ 1.48sg DHMW
       by 1600m MDbrt (prior to reaching the top error bar of the first overburden fault).
    •  MI to have a plan in place for weighting up on the fly.
    •   Hold PJSM with entire CDC crew covering proper PPE and procedures for handling LoTox Oil Based
      Mud (LTOBM).  Ensure all crews are briefed and are aware of the hazards on working with LTOBM
       mud. Also ensure adequate quantity of PPE suitable for OBM is available on the rig.
    •   Confirm MSDS for all MI chemicals on the rig are offshore
         o  The Last DAFWC on the Istiglal was due to SOBM exposure.
    •  Swaco to size shaker screens for cold LTOBM.
    •   Ensure that there are no discharge lines left open to the sea and the crews understand that no
     LTOBM mud goes overboard. Employ proper Lock Out Tag Out procedure

4)  Pressure test 22” casing.

    •   2,500 PSI surface pressure with 1.43 SG DHMW LTOBM
    •   This test is driven by 100bbl Gas Kick Profile with 0.24sg Kick Intensity Factor from deepest TD
         string is exposed (16-1/2” TD @ 4510m MDBRT)
    •  The 22” Surface Casing does NOT meet the drilling well control load case (burst) of “Gas to surface
       from 18” & 16” liner shoe fracture” (Casing Design Dispensation in place).

    •   Ensure all parties involved discuss, identify and confirm flow paths, pressures and potential leak
        paths.
    •  RECALCULATE PRESSURE TEST WITH ACTUAL FLUID DENSITIES

5)   Drill out shoe track and ream cement plus 3m new formation with 1.43sg DHMW LTOBM.

    •   Record choke line pressure loss prior to drilling out shoe
    •  Max WOB while drilling out Shoe track: 30Klb (limit to keep jars above the neutral point)
    •  The outer cutters on the 19.5” reamer have been modified to prevent excessive casing wear.
    •   Avoid rotating 17-1/4” stabilizer or 19-1/2” Rhino Reamer across the 16in hanger profile @ +/-1120m
       MDbrt and the 18in hanger profile @ +/-1220m MDbrt.  No interference expected while drilling
       shoe/cement based on BHA configuration and expected TOC. Verify space out once cement top is
        confirmed.
    •  Tag top of cement plug with the drill bit and pick up ~3m off bottom.
    •   Stage up to the drill out flow rate (~ 1,100gpm) and then rotate the tool slowly (30 to 50 RPM).
    •   Increase RPM until desired operating parameters are reached. Ream and wash down to the top of
        the cement. Drill the casing shoe track.
    •   Monitor for vibration while drilling out the 22” shoe. Adjust parameters as required to mitigate.


                       17-1/2” x 19-1/2” Drilling Parameter Acceptable Ranges
                  Circulation Rate (gpm)              1000 (T) - 1200 (P)
            Max WOB (klb)            30K (keep jars above the neutral point)
           RPM                                  ~60
            Max ROP (m/hr)                   as parameters dictate
           P = Pump Pressure Limit   T = Tool Limit

    •   Monitor magnets for metal – reduce drilling parameters if excessive metal shows.
    •  Back ream and re-ream every 5m.
    •  NOTE: be aware that  if cement is tagged high, there could be the situation where 19-1/2”
       Cleanout RR is drilling the cement in the shoe track while the assembly below is free rotating
         (off bottom) until the bottom of the rathole is tagged by the bit.   If cement is tagged high, and
       shoe track drilled, discuss the opportunity to RIH with pumps off and tag rathole TD for distance
          clarification. This will allow calculation of how much shoe track requires reaming with assembly off
       bottom and the ability to adjust reaming parameters accordingly.
    •   After drilling 3m of new formation, circulate and ensure clean returns.

6)  Perform Standard Leak Off Test (LOT):

    •  LOT at 22” shoe (assuming shoe set at 1,320m TVDBRT):
         o  The expected LOT, and minimum required, is 1.521 sg based on the fracture gradient
              model.   It will give 6 bbls KT and negative circulating MAASP (Dispensation in place – see
             comments below).
         o  A dispensation will be written in advance. The BP Drill Rep should ensure there is a signed
              copy of the dispensation on the rig before proceeding with the next section
         o  The acceptable LOT for compliance with BP Kick Tolerance Policy is 1.540 sg which
               provides a KT of 25 bbls with a circulating MAASP of 13 psi.
    •  LOT at 22” shoe (assuming shoe set at 1,400m TVDBRT):
         o  The expected LOT, and minimum required, is 1.549 sg based on the fracture gradient
              model.  It will give 37 bbls KT and 37 psi circulating MAASP.
    •  The maximum recommended FIT (if leak off is not observed) is 1.56 sg which complies with the
       acceptable LOT to get 25 bbls KT and provides an additional ECD margin.
    •     If LOT is below 1.521 sg (for 1320m TVDBRT) or 1.549 sg (for 1400m TVDBRT), discuss forward
        options with town (dispensation vs. squeezing 22” shoe). A contingency squeeze procedure will be
        available in advance.
    •   Refer to “SDX-5 LOT / ELOT Strategy” document for further details and procedure.
    •  Have “Designer Mud” pill available to spot across open hole to attempt to “Stress Cage” the weaker
        formations in the event the LOT is not acceptable.
    •  Do not drill ahead until the LOT results have been reviewed, interpreted and agreed with town team.
    •  [DIMS PHASE CHANGE TO LNR2]

7)   Drill to 52m below 22” shoe (42m of new hole – includes the 3m for LOT) to allow RR to be activated in
    the open hole and to ensure 19-1/2” Cleanout Reamer has cleared the shoe track and positioned in the
   open hole (rathole).

    •   Position the LOWER 22in. Rhino Reamer cutters (enlarging tool) at the top of the 17-1/2”.  Bit will be
        positioned 10m off bottom.
    •  Drop 2-1/4” ball to activate the LOWER 22in. Rhino Reamer.
    •   Verify opening by monitoring MWD turbine flow rate. (The MWD flow rate will reduce as flow is
        diverted out the Rhino Reamer jets).
    •   Rotate the tool slowly (30 to 50 RPM) and very slowly stage pumps up to the appropriate drill ahead
        flow rate to perform the cut out. Rotate while working the tool up and down approximately 3-5m until
       a cutout is established.
    •   Establish the cut out while noting weight and torque.
    •  Once the cut out is complete, with the pumps on and the rotary off, slowly lower the Rhino Reamer
       towards the bottom of the cutout.
    •   Weight should be seen on the indicator at the bottom of the cutout bench, verifying cutter block
         activation. Apply a maximum of 20K lbs of weight at the tool.

        Note: The bit should be off bottom at this time to ensure that the weight noted is at the 22in. Rhino
      Reamer cutter blocks.

        Note: A pull test at the casing shoe can be performed to verify that the cutters blocks are activated.
       Ensure the CMC is activated. DO NOT exceed 5K on the pull test.

    •    Drill off slowly while noting weight and torque
    •   Closely monitor surface vibration and down hole vibration.
    •     It is critical to have a good shoulder cut before proceeding. (SDX-4 LL’d)

8)  Underream until bit tags bottom (+/-5m). Use precaution as assembly below 22” RR will be free rotating.

9)   Drill ahead until the UPPER 19-1/2in Cleanout Rhino Reamer / Stabilizer is in the enlarged hole, and
    then proceed drilling to plan TD of 2620m MDbrt.

    •  Once both tools are in the new hole, the Rhino Reamers will be integral parts of the BHA, and should
            drill at bit parameters.
    •  The upper Rhino Reamer will act as a stabilizer.
    •   Rhino Reamer Operating Parameters: 96% flow to bit / 4% flow to lower RR / 0% flow to upper RR.
             If pump rate changes, have Smith perform new Hydraulics analysis to confirm tool operating
       parameters.
    •   Raise rig awareness of vibration and shock mitigation. Schlumberger D&M to provide a written
      summary of vibration and shock protocol to be used in decision making.
    •   While reaming,  if the bit is in a stringer, decrease WOB. When the reamer approaches the same
         stringer, decrease WOB and decrease RPM.   If the reamer is in a stringer and the bit is in a sand
        increasing WOB could have a tendency to buckle the drill string in the UR section.
    •   Minimize off bottom reaming. Excessive off bottom reaming can lead to twist off or back off.
    •  Reduce rotary speed prior to PU off bottom.

10) Drill 17 1/2” x 22” hole vertically to 2620m TVDbrt while building mud weight from 1.41sg SMW / 1.43sg
  DHMW to 1.46sg SMW / 1.48sg DHMW.

       NOTE: Achieve 1.48sg DHMW by 1600m MDbrt (prior to reaching the top error bar of the first
                overburden fault).

    •  Heightened awareness required for the management of mud properties, ECD, and Swab &
       Surge.
    •   Heightened awareness about drilling through a major fault

         o   Early indications  of rubble zone are  critical.   Geologist to monitor cutting returns  for
                 indications of fault penetration as well as trend analysis indicating the fault becoming less
                 stable.
         o  Minimize swab/surge effects through good hole cleaning and PWD/ECD monitoring.
         o   Monitor PWD signature for signs of erratic ECD spikes, indicating large formation fragments
                   in the annulus.
         o   Monitor and be prepared for “cuttings waves” at surface. May require multiple bottoms up to
                 circulate larger fragments out of the annulus.
         o   Erratic torque, a tendency  for packing  off and higher than usual P/U weights are  all
                 indications of rubble zone failure in the fault interval.
         o    If required to stop and circulate while drilling thru the fault zone, do not circulate at full drilling
                 flowrate within the fault zone. Pull above to circulate clean.
         o  Minimize Swab and Surge pressures while tripping through the fault interval
         o    If required to backream through the fault, proceed slowly with a pump rate sufficient only to
               clean the hole (swab and surge could further destabilize the hole).
    •   Maintain inclination at a minimum of <2 deg (under 1 deg if possible).  Inclination to be controlled by
        slacking off weight (control drilling) and maintaining high RPM to enhance the pendulum effect.
    •   Trip sheets shall be filled out by the driller on every trip in and out of the hole. Any deviation from
       expected hole fill up volumes shall be investigated.
    •   Update kick tolerance of the weakest known point of the hole section while drilling and record on all
     BP daily drilling reports. Update as required for any changes (MW, PPFG).
    •   Update a kick sheet daily and at every change in mud weight, bottom hole assembly (BHA) or
        formation integrity test.
    •     If losses occur discuss increasing / modifying LCM additions to the system while drilling.
    •   Raise rig awareness of vibration and shock mitigation. Schlumberger D&M to provide a written
      summary of vibration and shock protocol to be used in decision making.
    •   Record and monitor ECD from the PWD for real time usage. VH suggests adjusting flow rate within
        the acceptable drilling parameters has little effect on ECD.
    •  HOLE CLEANING:  Section can be drilled at 20-30 m/hr ROP with a 1.48sg DHMW, 1000 – 1100
      gpm and GOOD hole cleaning while maintaining an ECD of 1.504sg at TD and 1.500sg at shoe
       which is 0.02sg below the expected minimum open hole fracture strength (1.521sg @ 22” shoe).
    •     If the flowrate is reduced to 1000gpm, then reduce ROP to no more than 20m/hr.

17-1/2” x 22” Hole Section Hydraulics:
Bit: 17-1/2" RSX616M–A6, Bit Nozzles: 8 x 16, TFA=1.571, Rhino 16000 : Nozzle: 1 x 8, TFA=0.049
Based on ROP of 20m/hr
Flow Rate               1000              1100              1200*              1300*

SPP (psi)                2467              2886              3346              3843

ESD shoe                1.478               1.478               1.478               1.478

ESD td                   1.483               1.483               1.483               1.483

VH ECD shoe             1.500               1.498               1.497               1.496

VH ECD TD               1.504               1.502               1.501               1.500

     * Exceeds maximum pressure for 7” liner (3086psi 90% limit), however, SPP is modeled at TD so higher
    flow rates may be achievable in the shallower part of the section.

11) Drill 17 1/2” x 22” hole vertically to planned section TD of +/-2620m MD/TVDbrt while maintaining mud
    weight at 1.46sg SMW /1.48sg DHMW.

12) At TD circulate a minimum two times the open hole volume or until shakers are free of cuttings.

    •  TD should allow for 5m of 22” rathole beneath the 18” liner shoe (approximately 34m of total rathole
       based on 29m from bit to RR cutters – verify against as run BHA). This is enough rathole above the
       17 ½” pilot hole to account for any fill and be able to land the 18” liner hanger.
    •   Place a 1.9sg (DHMW) viscous pill in the rathole (34m) to prevent cement slumping.

13) POOH, rack back 6-5/8in DP and 9-1/2in Drill Collars. Prepare for wireline logging.

    •   6-5/8” DP, Record torque (10/20 rpm), pick-up, slack-off and rotational weights at TD
    •   Perform Swab/ Surge (GeoServices) calculation prior to POOH to determine max pulling speeds.
    •   Perform flowchecks while tripping out of hole: (1) When pulling off bottom (2) After pulling into the
        casing shoe (3) Before the BHA enters the BOP stack
    •    Driller to ensure hole fill volumes are correct every 5 stands or notify TP or WSL.
    •   Attempt to work through any tight spots first before reaming, back ream only if required.
    •   While pulling through the 22in casing with CMC active, pump at minimum rate for pipe displacement.
    •   Hole conditions will dictate if wiper trip is required.
    •  Once at surface, test the Rhino to make ensure tool is activating properly.

14) Run Formation Evaluation Logs

    •  WL Run 1: GR / EMS / GPIT
    •  WL Run 2: MDT / GR (extra large hole kit required)
    •  A qualified wireline logging witness will be offshore to oversee wireline jobs.
    •   Hole conditions will dictate if wiper trip is required.

15) Pull the 18-3/4” Wellhead Seat Protector (ID= 17.60 in.) prior to running 18” liner.

      7.1.5.6  18” Liner Running & Cementing Operations

1)  Run 18” Liner with auto-fill shoe (shoe at +/- 2560m tvd/MDbrt, Top of Liner (TOL) at +/- 1220m
    providing +/- 100m liner lap, 34m Rathole)

    •  REVIEW LEARNINGS FROM PREVIOUS WEATHERFORD SSR SYSTEM CEMENT JOBS
    •  Review and update Job Risk Assessments (JRA’s)
    •   Conduct PJSM before running casing.
    •   Rig team review the casing drop procedures developed for well control purposes and discuss with
       crews prior to liner running operations.

    •   18” liner can NOT be run closed ended without inducing losses at the open hole weak point (22”
       shoe @ 1.52sg) with a 1.48sg DHMW. The Surge Pressure / ECD running closed ended exceed the
       open hole weak point. NOTE: opportunity to optimize liner running strategy once LOT is obtained at
        22” Shoe.

    •   18” liner can be run open ended (no surge reduction tool included in string – see comment below).
      To maintain 1.51 ECD at 22” shoe (.01SG below the weak point), VH surge calculations suggests:
         o  0-1340m      Up to 1 minute per joint
         o  1340-1400m    5 mins/stand
         o  1400-1600m    10 mins/stand
         o  1600-1800m    15 mins/stand
         o  1800-2100m    20 mins/stand
         o  2100-2300m    15 mins/stand
         o  2300-2400m    12 mins/stand
         o  2400m-TD      10 mins/stand

        This assumes the use of autofill equipment. The estimated trip time is ~16.5 hrs. NOTE: the option /
        decision to include an inner string will be made after obtaining LOT results at 22” Shoe. Updated
       Tripping Schedule based on actual LOT, MW, and MW properties will be provided prior to
       running the 18” Liner.

         •  Check logs to confirm requirement for tripping autofill equipment prior to running through any
            Hydrocarbon bearing zones.  If autofill is tripped, fill pipe at least every four stands while RIH.
         •  Drop Weatherford autofill conversion ball before PU the running tool. With the ball on seat any
           pumping while RIH will trip the autofill equipment.

    •  Make up the Hydril 521 connections to 50,000ftlbs
    •    Install centralizers as per program (centralizer subs already m/u to full joints).
    •   Update Swab/ Surge (Geoservices) calculation prior to RIH with 18” Liner to determine max running
       speeds.
    •  The 18” hanger will be sent to the rig already made up to the running tool with two SSR cement
        wiper plugs installed below the hanger (refer to Planning / Preparations).
    •   Baker (3 dart) cement head loaded with the bottom cement drillpipe dart in the lower chamber,  the
        top cement drillpipe dart in middle chamber and hanger “dart” in the upper chamber. XOs supplied
       and drifted by Baker.
    •  Ensure all components in the cementing and landing string drift 2.935”
    •   Ensure work string and any crossovers are suitable for darts to pass. No square shoulders.
    •   Establish alignment of the BOP and Riser (INX2 LL #108).

2)  Land 18” liner in the rotary, change out to 5” DP elevators, PU Casing Hanger Running Tool (CHRT) with
    elevators and continue running 18” casing on 5,” S135, 34ppf landing string.

    •  Drop auto-fill conversion ball prior to p/u hanger (will not pass through Vetco dart sub or Weatherford
        wiper plugs).
    •   Verify the vertical painted stripe made in pre-ops checks on the running tool assembly is lined up.
    •  MU to casing string while verifying that nothing rotates in the running tool while making up to the
        casing string by watching the painted stripe.
    •  PU a few feet and record string weight

      o   18in Casing weight = +/-334k lbs
      o   Total String weight + 100k lbs over pull = +/-558k lbs
    •  The 5” 34ppf Landing string is required to run this casing string, driven by slip crushing loads.
    •  RIH filling pipe at least every four stands
    •   Ensure casing hanger and running tool are not across the BOP while making a connection.
    •  As per Vetco Rep instructions, land out casing at the 18” liner hanger sub in the 22” Casing, confirm
       depth and set down casing weight, holding landing string weight up on the tool.

   NOTE: The 18” liner will be across the BOP’s and in the OH while the liner hanger is picked up.
   Have procedures on the rig floor for dropping the 18” liner or  if circumstances allow running in hole to
    place DP across the BOP’s prior to closing.   Annulars can be closed on 18” liner, however, only at
    minimal closing pressure.

3) RU to circulate cement, establish circulation and condition the hole prior to pumping cement.

    •   Virtual Hydraulics indicates the casing can be circulated on bottom with 1.48sg DHMW at 500gpm
       (12bpm) without exceeding the open hole weak fracture pressure (assumed to be the 22” Shoe)
    •   Losses are “not probable” as Surge Pressure / ECD are predicted to be below the open hole weak
        point by +/- 0.028sg.
    •   Start circulation and stage up rates to cement displacement rates and reduce rate accordingly  if
        losses are experienced.
    •  Pump the cement job immediately after conditioning.

4)  Mix and pump cement as per cement program.
    •   18” liner will be cemented with a 1.60sg extended Lead slurry and 1.90sg Tail Neat G slurry system
         at 4-5bpm displacement with a 1.48sg DHMW.
    •   Planned Top of Lead is to the TOL at +/- 1220m and Top of Tail is 150m above 18” shoe.
    •  Cement job is subsea release (SSR) and not an inner string job. The SSR method minimizes the
        time until the liner is in place across the fault zone. Also minimizes the time the liner is across the
      BOP.
    •   Planned volumes assume 50% annular excess over gauged hole. Pump 10% excess over open hole
         caliper log volume (review caliper log and recalculate prior to job).
    •     If losses occur while running the liner discuss including CemNET in the slurry.
    •  Pump 80bbls of MUDPUSH spacer with rig pumps.
    •   Release the bottom dart
    •   Mix and pump Lead and Tail slurries at 1.60sg and 1.90sg of “G” Neat cement respectively at 4-
      5bpm with cement unit.
              o  Slow pump rate to 3-4bpm, before the dart contacts the bottom plug
    •   After pumping cement, launch top dart
    •   Start displacing with 10bbls MUDPUSH from cement unit followed by LTOBM until top dart lands out
       on top wiper plug.
              o  Slow pump rate to 3-4bpm before dart contacts the top plug
              o  Shear out top plug with cement unit
    •  Swap to rig pumps and displace cement with LTOBM
              o  Continue displacement at 6-8 bpm
              o  Spot 20 bbls MUDPUSH spacer across liner hanger
              o  Perform Hesitation Squeeze on last 100 bbls of displacement
                       Review INX and SDX procedures for hesitation squeeze.
              o  Bump top plug between 3-4bpm, final circulating pressure + 1000psi.
              o  Geoservices to monitor losses and final circulating pressure and record in DIMS
    •  TOC to be determined to an appropriate level. As a minimum, volumes pumped, volumes returned
       and differential pressure shall be recorded and reported.
    •   18” L42W Large Bore Auto-Fill Float Collar ratings: Back Pressure, 1700psi; Bump Pressure,
        1500psi; Conversion Pressure with ball on seat, 500- 700psi.
    •  Be prepared for cement returns to surface.

5)  Set seal assembly as per onsite Vetco rep instructions.

    •   Ensure all parties involved discuss, identify and confirm flow paths, pressures and potential leak
        paths.
    •   Set down 20Klbs on the tool and drop the dart
    •  Make four right hand turns on the drill pipe
    •   Pressure up through the drill pipe to 3000psi to set the seal. Do not exceed 3000psi. Hold for five
       minutes and then bleed off to zero psi.
    •  Open  drill sting to atmosphere, close pipe rams and pressure test the seal to 2300psi pressure
       through the choke and kill lines (this will provide the same downhole pressure that will be applied
        during the casing pressure test with 1.70sg MW). Do not exceed 4000psi test pressure. Hold test
       pressure for five minutes.
    •   Slowly bleed pressure to zero and open pipe rams, make four right hand turns on the running tool.
    •  PU approximately 4ft. to clear top of hanger with nose of tool.
    •   Pressure up DP to 4200psi to rupture dart. After rupture, do not exceed 3000psi circulating pressure
       through the 1in ruptured disc opening.
    •  Pump +/- 50 bbl scour pill to clean DP.

6)  POH, LD CHRT and rack back 5” 34ppf landing string.   If the 16” contingency liner is run the high
    capacity landing string will be required.

7)  RIH & Set 18 ¾” NSP

8)  Review requirement to test BOP stack.

7.1.6  16 ½” Hole, 13   ” x 13   ” Casing (Base Case - No 16” Liner) [LNR2 changing to INT1]

  7.1.6.1  Section Objectives / TD Criteria

•  TD the section 55m TVDBRT above the top of the error bar for Top Sabunchi (SE250). Using the
    current prognosis the section TD would be at 4,250m TVDBRT / 4,520 MDBRT (Current prognosis
     for Top Sabunchi  is 4,505m TVDBRT +/- 200m. Therefore top of the error bar  is at 4,305m
   TVDBRT). The 13-3/8” Casing would be set 10m off bottom at 4,240m TVDBRT / 4,510m MDBRT.
•   Set 13  ” far enough into the lower Surakhany to provide sufficient kick tolerance to drill the next
    hole section through the Sabunchi pressure ramp, yet avoid the higher pressured sands in the base
    Surakhany. These are expected to be ~ 40m TVD above the Sabunchi top (SE250).
•   Re-prognosis of formation depths and errors is required at the 18” liner shoe and also once seismic
    events SE230 and SE240 have been identified from LWD. This is required in an attempt to reduce
    the depth uncertainty, which will allow the casing depth to be pushed as deep as possible, without
    penetrating the high pressure sands in the lower Surakhany section.
•  Cement lifted to 300m MD above the permeable Upper Kjartan Sand (sand prognosed at 3072m
   TVDBRT +/-150m TVDBRT).

NOTE:   If the 18” casing shoe fracture pressure is lower than expected and pore pressures are higher
than expected (narrowing PPFG window) or in the event of insufficient kick tolerance to reach 4520m
MDbrt, or severe hole problems experienced drilling through the fault, then the 16” Contingency Liner will
be used. A 16 ½” x 19 ½” UR assembly would be required after setting the Liner.

  7.1.6.2  Hole Section Discussion / Risks / Mitigations

•   Faults
        o  The “Deep Fault” is expected at +/-3233m TVDbrt (-300m/+200m).
        o  The second, much larger fault (commonly called the deep fault) has clear displacement of
            up to 150 m max. In the SDX-4 well this seismic facies was associated with very low net
                to gross silts and shales with very little sand. On the seismic this fault disappears into the
             poor image zone below the Southeast Mud Volcano. This is a very large mud volcano (11
            sq km) and the point at which the fault enters the mud volcano, is near the edge and is not
                 likely to be  in contact with the actual mud which causes the image problem. The
              possibility of mud being present in the fault must be considered because while it has
            a very low probability,  it could have a huge negative event and may even result in
               sidetracking of the well. The E-02 well in the Chirag field encountered an overburden fault
               at roughly the same stratigraphic level and it was charged with high pressure mud. This
               resulted in 2 sidetracks before the drilling of the well was completed. While drilling the
               fault  interval, close monitoring  of  drilling parameters  will be  required  (flow
             monitoring, bit/BHA sticking).
        o  No other wells drilled to date in Shah Deniz have encountered any significant faults in the
             overburden section, thus limiting the ability to quantify the risk associated. Rigsite needs
              to be monitoring and prepared to react to potential problems associated with fault
              (torque, stuck pipe, losses, etc.).
        o  Base case directional plan completes the build section prior to encountering the fault at
             planned depth. But if the fault comes in at shallowest prognosis (2933m TVDbrt) then the
               build section will not be complete (end of build at 3081m TVDbrt).
        o   Drilling through the deep fault with the planned mudweight of 1.75SG is unlikely to cause
               losses, unless the ECD is significantly higher than the planned DHMW. The risk of lost
                circulation increases if the fault is penetrated shallower than planned. This risk decreases
               with depth.
        o   Lost Circulation Material is an option to prevent losses, but lowering ECD may be another
                solution. However, during discussions to reduce MW, it needs to be clear that reducing
            mudweight can enhance wellbore failure by breakout.
        o  The breakout analyses demonstrate that the planned mudweight of 1.75SG will result in
           some compressive failure through the fault zones. The breakout severity decreases if the
                faults are encountered shallow rather than deeper in the subsurface.

────────────────────────────────────────────
        o  The wellbore azimuth is oriented in the direction of SHmax, therefore breakout will occur
                 in the sides of the hole, which should be less problematic for hole cleaning
        o  The issue with the SDX-5 wellbore azimuth is that the fault strike and wellbore azimuth
             are close to parallel (i.e. approx E-W), so there is a risk of developing a long section of
           weakened rock by drilling a deviated hole through the deep fault that may cause problems
           when running casing.  If the hole remains open for a long time and the breakout is not
                inhibited by the mudweight, this could become a more serious problem. Mitigations would
              include minimizing open hole time and having the fill-up and circulating tool rigged up to
              allow washing through tight spots.
        o  Managing the  drilling risks through this fault interval  will require balancing downhole
            mudweight to  limit the risk of losses (which requires lower mudweight), yet keeping
            mudweight high enough to reduce breakout. Optimising hole cleaning procedures and
              monitoring cuttings volumes will be key as  it will be unlikely that zero breakout can be
             achieved (high MW required) without risking losses at the casing shoe or into the fault
             zone.

•   Lost Circulation
        o  Losses have occurred in offset wells in the weaker sand exposed at the top of the
            Surakhany, and down hole losses may be induced while drilling and running & cementing
              casing. The “Shah Deniz SDX-5 Lost Circulation Strategy” will be available for reference.
        o  Risk of lost circulation is elevated due to drilling through the Deep Fault.
        o   Drilling Fluid will be treated with LPM.
        o  Surge calculations to determine acceptable running speeds to minimize chances of losses

•   Wellbore Stability
        o MW for this interval will be above or equivalent to the recommended MW for the predicted
        WBS line.
        o   Monitor cuttings returns for indication of wellbore instability.
        o   Possible option to increase the MW. This must be discussed and agreed with town prior
               to taking action. Increasing the MW increases risks such as losses at the previous shoe
              (higher ECD) as well as increased instability across the fault interval (refer to the Fault
               section).

•   Pore Pressure Ramp / Tight Drilling Window
        o  Sand pressures begin to rise close to the base of the Surakhany. SDX-1 took a kick in one
               of the basal Surakhany sands (Sigurd-1 sand). These sands are expected to be ~ 40m
         TVD above the Sabunchi top (SE250). The hole section is planned to stop short of these
             sands, but vigilant monitoring should be adhered to in the event the sands are penetrated.
        o    If the 16-1/2” section is drilled too deep into the Sabunchi, high pressure sands will be
            exposed which may be difficult to control.
        o  The mud weight required to drill the pressure ramp creates high overbalance in the upper
               part of the section with potential for mud losses and differential sticking. The estimated
             overbalance at the previous shoe is around 1,445psi.
        o  Heightened awareness required for the management of mud properties, ECD, and Swab &
             Surge.

•   Excessive Casing Wear
        o  Raised rig awareness with respect to criticality of casing wear and influencing operational
               factors (dogleg severity & RPM).
        o  Ensure ditch magnets are used while drilling the 16-1/2” hole section. Ditch magnets
             should be monitored on a 12 hourly basis and results recorded for rig site trend analysis.

•   Directional Control
        o  The well will be kicked off from vertical up to 34 degrees of inclination.  Potential for poor
               directional control and high dog legs.
        o  The well trajectory has been optimised to penetrate the minimal number of faults.  The
           Deep Fault will be penetrated at the optimum angle to minimize the amount of drilling
             along the actual fault plane
        o  Refer to comments above in Faults section.

      7.1.6.3  Planning / Preparations

    •    Drill String: ~3150m 6   ” 27.7ppf S135 and ~1200m 5” 19.5ppf S135
    •   Landing String: N/A, fullbore casing job
    •   Rigsite Supervisors to review monitoring and first response procedures for potential
      problems associated with fault drilling (torque, stuck pipe, losses, etc) with rig crews. NOTE:
       Engineering Team to provide short presentation on fault drilling practices prior to drilling this
       hole section.
    •   Prior to drilling this section swap to 6” pump liners to be used for the remainder of the well. 90% of
      Maximum SPP rating for 6” liners is 4219psi.
    •   Ensure that strainers on mud pumps have been inspected and repaired prior to drilling ahead.
    •   Caliper ID on 10% of casing joints for use in cement displacement calculations (onshore inspection
        services to provide multi-armed caliper information for accuracy in displacement calculations).
    •  A minimum quantity of weighting material shall be available on the rig at all times to be able to
       weight up the circulating system by 0.12sg.
    •  A minimum supply of cement and cement additives shall be available on the rig at all times to be
        able to set appropriate isolation plugs.
    •  PREVUE to be installed / utilized for this section.
    •  The option / decision to include an inner string for the cement job will be made after obtaining LOT
         results at 18” Shoe combined with drilling  / wellbore conditions.  If decision made to cement with
        inner string, additional procedures will be issued to the offshore team.

    •   Ensure all crews are briefed and are aware of the hazards on working with LTOBM mud.
    •   Confirm MSDS sheets offshore.
    •   Ensure that there are no discharge lines left open to the sea and the crews understand that no
     LTOBM mud goes overboard.
    •   Record choke line pressure loss prior to drilling out shoe.
    •   Perform Well Control Drills

3)  Perform 18” Liner and Casing Hanger Seal Assembly pressure test.
    •  1900 PSI surface pressure with 1.70 SG DHMW
    •   This test is driven by 100bbl Gas Kick Profile with 0.24sg Kick Intensity Factor from deepest TD
         string is exposed (16-1/2” TD @ 4510m MDBRT)
    •   Ensure all parties involved discuss, identify and confirm flow paths, pressures and potential leak
        paths.
    •  RECALCULATE PRESSURE TEST WITH ACTUAL FLUID DENSITIES


4)   Drill out 18” shoe track plus 3m new formation.
    •  Once floats valves are drilled out potential exist for exposure to formation pressure.

5)  Perform Extended Leak Off Test (ELOT) / Formation Integrity Test (FIT).
    •  The expected LOT, and minimum required, is 1.806 sg based on the fracture gradient model.
        This will provide 79 bbls KT and 56 psi circulating MAASP.
    •  The acceptable LOT for compliance with BP Kick Tolerance Policy is 1.792 sg which provides a
      KT of 62 bbls with a circulating MAASP of 4 psi and an ECD margin of 0.022sg. Below this LOT
        value, the MAASP would become negative.  If LOT is below 1.792 sg then discuss forward
        operations with town (dispensation vs. squeezing 18” shoe).
    •  The maximum recommended FIT  (if leak  off  is not observed)  is 1.894 sg which  is the
       overburden. This complies with the minimum acceptable LOT to obtain 25 bbls KT and provides
       an additional ECD margin.
    •  Have “Designer Mud” pill available to spot across open hole to attempt to “Stress Cage” the
       weaker formations in the event the LOT is not acceptable.
    •   Refer to “SDX-5 LOT / ELOT Strategy” document for further details and procedure.
    •  Do not drill ahead until results have been discussed with town.

6)   Drill 16 ½” hole vertically to kick off point with RSS assembly (KOP=2,600m TVD brt / MDbrt), then
    build inclination at 2.0 deg/30m to final tangent angle of 34 deg at 3081m TVDbrt / 3110m MDbrt and
    hold 34 deg to section TD (+/-4250m TVDbrt / 4520m MDbrt). [DIMS PHASE CHANGE TO INT1]

    Start drilling the 16 ½” section with 1.68sg SMW  / 1.70sg DHMW and build the weight to 1.73sg
  SMW / 1.75sg DHMW.

    NOTE: Achieve 1.75sg DHMW by 2900m MDbrt (prior to reaching the top error bar of the second
            overburden fault).

    •  Heightened awareness required for the management of mud properties, ECD, and Swab &
       Surge.
    •  A FOSV complete with appropriate crossovers shall be available on the drillfloor at all times.
    •   Trip sheets shall be filled out by the driller on every trip in and out of the hole. Investigate any
        deviation from expected hole fill-up volumes.
    •   Determine and record choke line pressure losses (1) Prior to drilling out casing (2) On any
         significant change in mud weight
    •   Continuously update kick tolerance of the weakest known point of the hole section while drilling
       and record on BP daily drilling reports.
    •   Update a kick sheet daily and at every change in mud weight, bottom hole assembly (BHA) or
        formation integrity test.
    •   Heightened awareness about drilling through a major fault
      o   Early indications  of rubble zone are  critical.   Geologist to monitor cutting returns  for
             indications of fault penetration as well as trend analysis indicating the fault becoming less
             stable.
      o  Minimize swab/surge effects through good hole cleaning and PWD/ECD monitoring.

         o   Monitor PWD signature for signs of erratic ECD spikes, indicating large formation fragments
                   in the annulus.
         o   Monitor and be prepared for “cuttings waves” at surface. May require multiple bottoms up to
                 circulate larger fragments out of the annulus.
         o   Erratic torque, a tendency  for packing  off and higher than usual P/U weights are  all
                 indications of rubble zone failure in the fault interval.
         o    If required to stop and circulate while drilling thru the fault zone, do not circulate at full drilling
                 flowrate within the fault zone. Pull above to circulate clean.
         o  Minimize Swab and Surge pressures while tripping through the fault interval
         o    If required to backream through the fault, proceed slowly with a pump rate sufficient only to
               clean the hole (swab and surge could further destabilize the hole).
        •     If losses occur discuss increasing / modifying LCM additions to the system while drilling.
        •   Allow for a minimum 10m of rat hole below the 13   ” casing. This should be enough rat hole to
           account for fill and be able to land the casing hanger on the wellhead.
        •  GOOD hole cleaning can be achieved at 15-20 m/hr ROP and 850gpm, the predicted ECD at
            the previous shoe of 1.783sg  will remain below the expected minimum open hole fracture
            strength (1.806sg at 18” shoe).
        •  Do not control drill. Adjust accordingly to PWD readings.

7)  At TD circulate a minimum two times the open hole volume or until shakers are free of cuttings.

    •  TD should allow for a 10m rathole beneath the 13   ” shoe.
    •   Condition mud prior to POOH to run casing.
    •   Place a 1.90sg (DHMW) viscous pill on bottom, to prevent cement slumping into the rat hole
       (10m).

8) POOH, R/B BHA, prepare for wireline logging

    •   Lay down BHA components not required in the next hole section off the critical path.
    •  Swab  / Surge (GeoServices) calculation to be performed prior to POOH to determine max
         pulling speeds.
    •   Perform flowchecks while tripping out of hole: (1) When pulling off bottom (2) After pulling into
        the casing shoe (3) Before the BHA enters the BOP stack
    •   Wiper trip only to be performed if hole conditions dictate.

    •  WL Run 2: MDT / GR

    •  A qualified wireline logging witness will be offshore to oversee wireline jobs.
    •  A qualified VSP witness will be offshore to oversee VSI checkshot and VSP job
    •   Wiper trip only to be performed if hole conditions dictate.

      7.1.6.6  Casing Running and Cementing Operations

NOTE: The option / decision to include an inner string for the cement job will be made after obtaining LOT
results at 18” Shoe combined with drilling / wellbore conditions.  If decision made to cement with inner string,
additional procedures will be issued to the offshore team.

1)  Run 13 3/8” x 13 5/8” Casing (shoe at +/- 4240m TVDbrt / 4510m MDbrt).

    •   Planned string weight at TD in 1.75sg mud  is +/-1049klbs.  Rig SWL  / limitation is 1200klbs,
        providing 150klbs overpull.
    •   Casing will be run with Vetco Full-bore Casing Hanger RT and 13 5/8” casing landing string.
    •   Casing Hanger / Running tool to be pre-assembled and drifted to 12-1/4” onshore as follows:
         o  +/-6m Pup Joint – 13-5/8” Vam SLIJ-II, 88.2lb/ft
         o  13 5/8''FBCHRT
         o   13-5/8" Fullbore Casing Hanger
         o  3m Pup Joint - 13-5/8” Vam SLIJ-II, 88.2lb/ft
    •   Fullbore Cement Head SureLock Adapter will be M/U to 13-5/8” landing joint onshore.
    •   Ensure that the correct water bushing is on the drill floor at all times to be able to circulate through
        casing. First option is to use the Weatherford fill up tool
    •  Do not exceed 3 BPM circulating rate (autofill float collar converts at 5-8 BPM).    If required to
         circulate at higher than 3 BPM, discuss with town prior to tripping floats.  This will affect the casing
        running speed due to the conversion to closed-ended casing running.
    •  Swab/ Surge (MI’s Virtual Hydraulics & GeoServices) calculation to be performed prior to RIH with
       13 3/8” x 13 5/8” casing to determine max running speeds.
    •   Ensure all wear bushings / NSPs have been removed (pump down kill line and monitor for pressure
        increase as NSP passes by for confirmation of good recovery).
    •  Do not exceed optimum casing MU Torques: 13 5/8” = 34.4k ft-lb and 13-3/8” = 27.1k ft-lb.
    •     If casing not taking correct volume, break circulation as the filter in the shoe track may be plugged.
    •  Check logs and trip auto-fill equipment prior to running through any Hydrocarbon bearing zones
    •   Ensure the 13 5/8” x 13 3/8” XO is positioned at the previous casing shoe (18” liner)
    •    Install centralizers as per casing tally.
    •   Establish alignment of the BOP and Riser.

2)  Run 13 5/8” x 13 3/8” casing on 13 5/8” casing running/landing string.

    •   With last joint of casing in the rotary, PU casing hanger assembly.
    •   Target MU Torques for the landing string joints: 13 5/8” = 35.4k ft-lb and 13 3/8” = 28.1k ft-lb. (1k ft-
         lb more than casing below the hanger)
    •  Lower casing with hook unlocked and heave compensator adjusted to support all but 5,000lbs of the
        running string weight.
    •   Note string weight prior to landing casing
    •  Land casing in wellhead housing, compare depth to depth recorded when pulling wear bushing.

3)  Establish circulation and condition the hole prior to pumping cement.

    •     If not already done, trip autofill equipment by circulating to applying 500 to 700psi at the tool (trapped
         ball assembly).
    •   Start circulation at 1 bpm and stage up to maximum displacement rate of cement job.
    •   Circ annular volume x 1.5 while preparing for cementing operations.
    •  Pump the cement job immediately after conditioning.

4)  Mix and pump cement as per cement program
    •   Planned volumes below assume 50% annular excess over gauged hole. Pump 20% excess over open
        hole caliper log volume (review caliper log and recalculate prior to job).
    •   Displacement Volume  calculations based  on:  theoretical volume  plus  1/3 shoe  track,  plus mud
        compressibility, assuming 95% mud pump efficiency, and using callipered pipe ID. This volume has
       worked well for previous SD wells where plugs were bumped (recalculate prior to job).
    •  TOC to be 300m above the Upper Kjartan Sand (prognosed at +/-3072m TVDBRT). Geologist to confirm
       from logs while drilling hole section.
    •  DO NOT pump CemNET for this cement job  if running the MudMaster Filter Shoe.   Possibility of
     CemNET plugging the MudMaster Filter Shoe (SDA-05 lesson learned).
    •   Displace cement with mud weight used to drill this section. Next section mud weight is heavier than the
       cement and if plugs fail a wet shoe would result due to U-Tubing.
    •  Pump 100bbl MUDPUSH, 6bpm
    •   Release Bottom non-rotating cement plug after pumping spacer.
    •   Mix and pump 1.90SG Tail slurry as per cement program.
    •   Release Top non-rotating cement plug.
    •   Displace 10bbl MUDPUSH with cement until to clear lines
    •  Swap to rig pumps and continue displacement with LTOBM, 8bpm
         o  Slow pump rate to 3bpm  just before bottom plug bump.  Record plug diaphragm rupture
                pressure. 13 3/8” HP NR Plug Set – rupture rating of Bottom Plug Rupture @ 1,000psi
    •  Reduce rate to 3-4bpm and bump top plug with final circulating pressure +1000psi. 13 3/8” L45WP Float
        Collar ratings: Back Pressure: 3000psi; Bump Pressure 5000psi; Conversion Rate: 500 - 700psi.
    •   Determine TOC to an appropriate  level. As a minimum, volumes pumped, volumes returned and
         differential pressure shall be recorded and reported.
    •  Do not pick up or rotate the running string while circulating or cementing.

5)  Release Full Bore Casing Hanger running tool as per Vetco onsite rep & lay down 13 5/8” landing string.
    •   Flush choke and kill lines immediately after cementing
    •   Flush at least two times the riser volume
    •   While circulating take 5000lbs overpull, place tongs on running string and rotate to the right maintaining
         overpull. Rotate running string 2 to 2 ½ turns to the right to release running tool
    •   Retrieve running tool.

6)  Run MS Seal assembly for the casing hanger on drillpipe (DP).

7)  Set seal assembly as per Vetco instructions and Pressure test.
    •   Pressure test to 3300 psi (surface pressure).
    •   Ensure all parties involved discuss, identify and confirm flow paths, pressures and potential leak paths.

8)  Run and set 13 5/8” wear bushing.

9)  Run BOP Isolation Test Tool (BOPITT) and perform  full BOP test (review BOP testing requirements for
    possible drillahead opportunities).
    •   Function test BOPITT at the rotary, reset tool prior to running.
    •   Prior to test tool entering the BOP, activate the compensator.
    •   Verify landing depth
    •   Pressure Test Rams to 10,000 psi and Annulars to 5,500 psi (surface pressure) with 1.75 sg DHMW.

10) Pressure Test 13 3/8” x 13 5/8” casing.
    •   3,300 PSI surface pressure with 1.75 SG DHMW
    •   This test is driven by 100bbl Gas Kick Profile with 0.24sg Kick Intensity Factor from deepest TD string is
       exposed (12-1/4” TD @ 5,630m MDBRT)
    •   Ensure all parties involved discuss, identify and confirm flow paths, pressures and potential leak paths
    •  RECALCULATE PRESSURE TEST WITH ACTUAL FLUID DENSITIES

11) Commence operations to change out 10K psi WP Riser Joints to 15K psi WP Joints.

 8.3  Rupture Disk Sub Placement

“C” Annulus – 13-5/8” Casing x 22” Casing
    22” Casing: An outward acting burst disc installed in the 22” casing will be employed to address the
     collapse concern of the 13-5/8” casing. 1x Burst Disc sub placed below 18 ¾” HP wellhead crossover
      joint – approximately 20m below mudline. Burst Disc outward Pressure Rated to 5000psi +/- 5% @
    150oF, 4871psi to 5384psi @ 72oF.



“D” Annulus - Contingency 16” Liner x 18” Liner
    16” Contingency Liner: A collapse disc installed below the liner hanger in the 16” liner will be employed
     to address the collapse concern of the 16” liner. Place below first full length casing joint below 16”
     casing hanger. Collapse Disc pressure rated to 1,200 psi ± 5% at 100°F with a minimum back pressure
     of 6,300 psi.



“B” Annulus – 10-3/4” - 10” Casing x 13-5/8” Casing
   No mitigations in order, the Safety factors for this string are close to the Design factors.



“A” Annulus – Tubing x 10-3/4” - 10” Casing
   No mitigations in order, the Safety factors for this string exceed the Design factors.

 LWD requirements - 17 ½” x 22” hole

           1330 – 2620 mMDbrt
        ARC – PWD (Gamma-Resistivity-PWD)

            Refer to Hole Interval Decision Analysis / Tree for tool failure pulling decisions


  Wireline Logging Requirements 17 ½” x 22” hole

        GR – EMS - GPIT

          MDT- GR Pressures only. (Extra large Hole Kit Required)

            GR     Gamma Ray
            EMS      6-Arm Calliper
               GPIT       Orientation and Inclination
            MDT      Pressure Measurement


          First run is definitive depth for well. Subsequent wireline runs calibrated to this.
       Repeat Section to be c. 100 m near TD at start of up-log.
        Logging witness required in the wireline unit when in open hole.

       Tool notes
     mud will be the logging medium.
         Full backup of same tools required.
        Fishing kit to be available on the rig.
       Every component must be callipered prior to running in the hole.
       Perform tool checks at surface.
       Approach TD with care. There are two objectives at this point – maximize the amount
         of data by not ending the down-log too early and starting the up-log well away from TD.
      And secondly not sitting on TD for any longer than necessary to establish loss of
        neutral tool weight.
      Down log to be recorded at 15 – 20 m/min until neutral weight is established.
       Stop recording down-log and come out of the hole slowly while preparing tools / data-
          files for up-log.
      Once system ready for up-log, return to TD slowly.
      Tag TD again and come out of the hole slowly, open calipers and start recording.
       Perform repeat section prior to main log.
       Log GR to surface.

 12.2 BOP
Specifications:

21” x 50’ Vetco MR6-D riser complete with (2) 3” ID 15,000 psi WP H2S trim kill and choke lines; (1) 4” ID
5000 psi WP Booster line.

NOTE:  Due to the water depth and lack of sufficient joints, a portion of the riser will consist of 10,000 psi
      WP joints down to the 13-3/8” casing setting point.  At that point, riser joints will be pulled and
         replaced with 15,000 psi WP.

18 ¾” 15,000psi BOP stack and Lower Marine Riser Package consisting of:

LMRP:

18-3/4” Hydril GX 10,000psi Annular BOP (1)

BOP Stack:
Hydril 18-3/4” 10,000psi Annular BOP (1)
Hydril 18-3/4” 15,000psi WP double ram preventors (2) fitted as follows (top to bottom):
    •  Top Rams           Blind / Shear Rams
    •  Upper Rams        5” x 7” Variable Bore Rams
    •   Middle Rams        5” Fixed Pipe Rams
    •  Lower Rams         3-1/2” x 5-1/2” Variable Bore Rams

 12.3 BOP and Casing Test Pressures

    12.3.1 36” Conductor / 28” Liner
   The 36” string is structural pile and not for pressure containment.  The 28” liner is not for pressure
    containment. Pressure testing is not required.

    12.3.2 BOP Surface Stump Test

             BOP Component        Test Pressure (psi)
                           Annular                      7,000
                         Pipe Rams                    10,000
                       Shear Rams                   10,000


         •  The stump test will serve as the primary BOP test for the 17-1/2” x 22” hole interval.
         •   After running the BOP, the Wellhead Connector test will be done to 10,000psi Surface
          applied pressure with seawater as test fluid (limited by C&K lines of the riser joints on
           loan from DDGG).
         •   After the 10K psi Riser Joints have been replaced with the 15K psi Riser Joints, the
       BOP Connector will be pressure tested to 10,000psi Surface applied pressure with
          seawater as test fluid.

    12.3.3 BOP Test Summary
         •   22" BOP Tests are surface stump tests*.
         •   Pressure tests values are applied at surface
         •   Fluid densities are Down Hole Mud Weight (DHMW) NOT Surface Mud Weights
         •   Pipe ram pressure tests are based on MASP derived from Fracture at Shoe well control load
           case with water
         •   Casing pressure tests are based on MASP derived from 100bbl, 0.24SG KI Gas Kick Profile
             (22” to10”)

 15  Casing Design - Casing Wear Strategy

A strategy to mitigate against and evaluate excessive casing wear was put in place on SDA-01. A baseline
Multi-Finger Caliper Tool (MFCT) was run inside the 10-3/4" x 10" casing and a post drilled MFCT run after
+/- 500 krevs.  The two logs indicated that virtually no wear had occurred during this time.  Part of the
procedure was to use CWEAR software to back out wear factors from the casing wear signature. This
proved to be meaningless due to negligible wear occurring.  During drilling and coring of the 8½" section
metal returns from the ditch magnets versus cumulative revs was recorded.  This provided a qualitative
measure of casing wear against time and provides a baseline to compare all future wells against.

A final MFCT was also run after the 5-1/2” liner was set on SDA-01 to further evaluate actual wear during
slow drilling 8-1/2” section to TD. Again negligible casing wear was observed.

A new strategy was implemented in SDX-4. Two USIT logs were run to evaluate the casing wear on the 10”
casing due to some concerns regarding its integrity prior to the well test because the extensive rotating hours
that the casing was exposed to.  Finally, the Cwear software (vr 6.2) was run to predict the casing wear on
the 10” casing prior to the final casing integrity test for the well test.

    •  A thorough process was carried out to be able to calibrate the Cwear model and obtain the
        appropriate wear factors based on the first USIT log.
         o  The 10” casing was run and cement on May 14th, 2006.
         o  The first USIT log was run on September 17th, 2006. The estimated total rotating hours on
                the casing were ~ 300 hrs and the maximum observed casing wear was 15.7%.

    •  Once the first calibration was done, the wear factors were verified using the second USIT log. Good
       match on the both wear models were observed.
         o  The second USIT log was run on February 26th, 2007. The estimated total rotating hours on
                the casing were ~ 440 hrs and the maximum observed casing wear was 16.6%.

    •   Finally, using the calibrated wear factors, the expected casing wear on the 10” casing was predicted.
         o  The analysis was done on July 28th, 2007. The estimated total rotating hours on the casing
             were ~ 585 hrs and the maximum predicted casing wear in the interest area was 20%.

The above results from SDX-4 were used to predict the casing wear in SDX-5 for the 10-3/4” x 10” casing
considering a good range of rotating hours (200, 400 and 600 hours). The results of this prediction indicate
that the 8-1/2" section in SDX-5 can be drilled without casing wear protection.

Casing wear is a function of drill pipe hard banding, wall force and rotating hours. The depth of the Shah
Deniz reservoir leads to high drillpipe tensions. These tensions will create high wall forces around planned
and unplanned doglegs. The 10 3/4” x 10” production casing is the most critical string to casing wear due its
depth, the length of exposure time while drilling the subsequent 8-1/2” section and the production loads that
this casing requires to stand.

Casing wear is highest at the surface where the tensions are highest and decreases with depth. It is critical
for casing wear (as well as torque and drag) to minimise doglegs near surface.

The graph below gives an indication of the casing wear on 10 3/4” x 10” casing for the SDX-5 well.

The burst strength of the casing is given by:

         Burst with wear = API Burst * (1 – %wear/100)

The maximum allowable wear on the 10 3/4” x 10” casing has been taken into account during the casing
design to ensure it does not exceed the predicted casing wear using the Cwear Vr. 6.2 software

Casing Wear recommendations for SDX-5

    •   Ensure awareness raised on rig with respect to criticality of casing wear and influencing operational
        factors (dogleg severity & RPM).
    •   Ensure ditch magnets are used while drilling the 16-1/2”, 12-1/4” and 8-1/2” hole sections. Ditch
       magnets should be monitored on a 12 hourly basis and results recorded for rig site trend analysis.
    •     If excessive metal is seen at surface and / or rotating hours exceed modeled limits, consider running
       a casing wear evaluation log (USIT log).
