 19  Challenges, Risks and Contingencies

 19.1  Marine/ Logistics’ Prioritisation
The Istiglal rig will be operating during a high demand period for marine vessels and helicopter utilization.
These conditions may impact the supply of materials or dedicated vessels for drill cuttings transport to the
Istiglal. The utilization of the marine fleet will be actively managed.

 19.2  Shallow Gas
There are no indications of shallow gas accumulations within a 300m radius of the well trajectory within the
tophole section. ML to depth of 1320m TVDBRT - identified no instances of shallow gas accumulations within a
300m radius of the well location. Therefore the risk of encountering a shallow gas accumulation is considered
to be Negligible. 1320m TVDBRT to 1523m TVDBRT (+/-51m) – small amplitude anomaly will be intersected
at 1452m TVDBRT (+/-47m). This is below the 22” casing shoe so will be drilled with weighted mud and BOPs.
The risk of encountering a shallow gas accumulation in this interval is considered to be Low.

 19.3  Shallow Water Flows
Overpressured water or brine sands have proved problematic in a high proportion of wells drilled in the South
Caspian Basin. The SGA states that no overpressures are predicted for the tophole section.  But a detailed
review of shallow pressure (April 2008) has indicated that SWF from the ‘Running Sands’ (predicted in the
interval 834±18m and 911±22m TVDSS in SDX-5; which have provided a source for shallow water flow and
gas in offset wells) is LIKELY.

 19.4  Shallow Faults
No major active or inactive faults occur within a 300m radius of either well trajectory from seabed to the limit of
the SGA investigation at 1500±51m TVDSS.

 19.5  Unconsolidated, Weak or Flowing Layers
There is a Low probability of tight hole conditions whilst drilling the Palaeo flow deposits, which occur at eight
levels within the shallow section. There is also a Likely risk of encountering flowing sands within the ‘Running
Sands’ interval which will be encountered between 834±18m and 911±22m TVDSS in SDX-5. This is mainly
due to the fact that the Q Sands will be drilled underbalanced. Pad Mud will be used to hold back the flow as
well as a cement design to accomplish the same. Also reviewing the option to close off the cement ports after
the cement is in place to provide back pressure while cement is setting.

 19.6 Mud Volcanoes
Two active mud volcanoes occur within the Shah Deniz area. These are 8km NW of location and 12km to the
WSW. There is considered to be a Negligible risk of flows from these reaching the SDX-5 location.

On seismic, the second, much larger fault (commonly called the deep fault) disappears into the poor image
zone below the Southeast Mud Volcano. This is a very large mud volcano (11 sq km) and the point at which the
fault enters the mud volcano, is near the edge and is not likely to be in contact with the actual mud which
causes the image problem. The possibility of mud being present in the fault must be considered because
while it has a very low probability, it could have a huge negative event and may even result in sidetracking of
the well.

 19.7 Pore Pressure / Fracture Gradient
SDX-5 is expected to be highly overpressured with pressure ramps and regressions, making drilling conditions
difficult.

The planned surface location for SDX-5 is approximately 2082m to the east-southeast of the reservoir target. A
deviated well path has been selected in order to move the penetration points of potentially high pressure sands

      Shah Deniz D&C                       SDX-5 Operations Drilling Program                       Rev1.04
       FINAL DOCUMENT LOCATION: http://bak-cpol.bpweb.bp.com/livelink/llisapi.dll/open/7395632

                                                      150


────────────────────────────────────────────
[ صفحه 151 از 160 ]
────────────────────────────────────────────
within the overburden down-dip and thereby provide a wider Pore Pressure-Fracture Pressure window to a
certain extent. The location was also chosen to minimize the PP/FG window (in the Surakhany interval) in an
attempt to prove up the ability to drill closer to the targets for Stage-2 (thus reducing wellbore inclination).

The first anticipated pressure ramp occurs between the first and second Surakhany anhydrite (between Top
Surakhany and the se220 pick). The pressures are predicted to increase from 1.4 sg to 1.6 sg. The second
major pressure ramp occurs below the Top Sabunchi shale around 4450m TVDBRT where the pressure is
expected to increase from 1.8 sg to 1.9 sg. Below Top Balakhany, the pressures are expected to decrease
gradually from 1.9sg to 1.57 sg before entering the reservoir section.

The reservoir section should be drilled overbalanced to stay above the unregressed SP1 pressures of around
1.74sg (5615m to 5670m TVDBRT). Particular caution should be used while drilling and logging this section as
the high overbalance can cause problems such as differential sticking or losses  if the formation fracture
pressure is exceeded.

 19.8  Reservoir Pressures / Regression
The sandstones in the reservoir are regressed, and therefore the fracture pressure  will also be reduced,
increasing the possibility of mud losses.  Contingencies will be available, such as the use of stress cage
procedures and perhaps the need to case off the higher pressure interval above.

 19.9  Wellbore Stability
Tectonic stresses can induce modifications in pore pressures, breakout and wellbore stability problems.

SDX-5 will not exceed 34 degrees inclination. A WBS study has been conducted on the proposed SDX-5 well-
bore. No significant WBS hazards were identified. The MW’s are above the minimum recommended weights
for WBS.

The principal risk as seen in Shah Deniz is from squeezing sands, which demand a careful regime of reaming
and good drilling practices. Caliper data will be acquired during the drilling of the well to update the WBS
model. A Pore Pressure specialist will monitor WBS in addition to the mudloggers who will monitor and report
the presence of cavings. Cavings generated by tectonic stress and breakout are usually blocky whilst
overpressure cavings are usually platy or long / thin and possibly spindled.

Another key risk for SDX-5 related to WBS will be the drilling of the 2 major faults.  As mentioned above,
mudloggers will need to monitor cuttings for indications of WBS issues related to the faults.

 19.10   Deeper Faults (below 1500m TVDBRT)
No other wells drilled to date in Shah Deniz have encountered any significant faults in the overburden section,
thus limiting the ability to quantify the risk associated.  Rigsite needs to be monitoring and prepared to react to
potential problems associated with fault (torque, stuck pipe, losses, etc.). ]

Lost Circulation Material is an option to prevent losses, but lowering ECD may be another solution. However,
during discussions to reduce MW, it needs to be clear that reducing mudweight can enhance wellbore failure by
breakout.

Managing the drilling risks through the fault interval will require balancing downhole mudweight to limit the risk
of losses (which requires lower mudweight),  yet keeping mudweight high enough  to reduce breakout.
Optimising hole cleaning procedures and monitoring cuttings volumes will be key as it will be unlikely that zero
breakout can be achieved (high MW required) without risking losses at the casing shoe or into the fault zone.

 19.11   Conductor Slumping / Cratering
Analyses of the Exploration & Pre-drill wells in Shah Deniz suggest that conductor slumping has not been a
problem to-date. On SDX-2 the conductor was run to 230m below mud-line and cemented with conventional
Lead/Tail slurry followed by top-up job and NO conductor slumping problems were encountered. On all 4 Pre-
drill wells the conductor was run +/- 50m below mud-line and cemented in place with conventional Tail slurry
followed with a top-up cement job and again NO conductor slumping problems were evident. On SDX-4 the


      Shah Deniz D&C                       SDX-5 Operations Drilling Program                       Rev1.04
       FINAL DOCUMENT LOCATION: http://bak-cpol.bpweb.bp.com/livelink/llisapi.dll/open/7395632

                                                      151


────────────────────────────────────────────
[ صفحه 152 از 160 ]
────────────────────────────────────────────
conductor was run to 134m below mud line and cemented with Class G neat lead and tail slurries mixed at 1.5
SG and 1.9 SG respectively.  It was decided to pump 80 bbls of slurry on top-up job due to expected cratering
tendency and NO conductor slumping problems were encountered.On INX-2 the 36” Conductor was cemented
with conventional Lead/Tail slurry and followed by top-up cement job. The wellhead required a tail slurry is
designed to be brought up a min of 50m above the shoe.

The 16m surface sand that is present at the E2 platform location does not exist at SDX-5 location. Therefore
cratering tendency around conductor is considered to be low at SDX-5 location. To mitigate against conductor
slumping in case of crater develops around the conductor it is planned to fill up the crater around the conductor
with cement to the mud-line.

 19.12   Mud Weight Selection for WBS / Overbalance / Kick Tolerance/ ECD
All the drilling risks associated with the previous Shah Deniz wells are applicable to SDX-5. These risks are
primarily related to the pressure regime, with the likely presence of regressed and overpressured sandstones
interbedded with overpressured mudstones. These conditions may provide a limited PP-FG window, with the
potential for wellbore ballooning and the possibility of some wellbore breakout. Careful attention to mud
conditions and drilling practices will be essential for management of the mud ECD.

 19.13   Mud Losses
The narrow PP-FP window in the deeper parts of the well carries with it the risk of fracturing the formation and
inducing mud losses.

Analysis of the offset data suggests that massive mud losses while drilling or logging has not been a problem to
date, but seepage losses have been observed. Losses while running and cementing casing have been a major
issue on the predrill wells and is a strong possibility on this well given the tight tolerance casing configuration
and the resultant clearances.

The losses described above occur due to the Pore/MW/Frac regime experienced on Shah Deniz.  Strict
management of ECD, Surge & Swab during drilling and cementing will be essential to minimize losses.

 19.14    Rig Reliability
Historically over the 10 wells drilled to date on Shah Deniz, including SDX-4, the Istiglal has had problems with
major pieces of equipment (Top Drive, BOP’s, Engine’s, Draw works, Rotary table) due to the harsh drilling
environment. This remains a potential risk for significant downtime.

 19.15   Data Acquisition
Historically on Shah Deniz, TD logs have mainly been run on TLC. To date TLC logs have never become stuck
on Shah Deniz. Results when using wireline however have been mixed and fishing jobs have resulted on many
occasions.

The base plan for SDX-5 is to run wireline logs. The TLC option is kept as contingency if wireline logs can not
obtained.

The option to perform TLC logging must be weighed against the cost. Typically a TLC logging job will take 2 - 3
times as long to perform than conventional wireline. There is therefore a large prize in terms of rig time and
hence cost to have the ability to run wireline logs in these holes.

 19.16    Stuck Pipe
Exploration drilling experience has shown that stuck pipe is a major drilling risk especially in the reservoir
section. Two-stuck pipe instances occurred during the Shah Deniz exploration programme while drilling SDX-1
and SDX-3 reservoirs. The cause of the stuck pipe is believed to be squeezing sand sections. The squeezing
sands in the Lower Surakhany were one of the contributing factors to the stuck pipe event on SDA-03.

Based on learning from the Shah Deniz program and subsequent WBS studies it has been concluded that the
best ways to avoid stuck pipe due to these squeezing sands is:


      Shah Deniz D&C                       SDX-5 Operations Drilling Program                       Rev1.04

    •   Optimised BHA design (via use of RSS systems, active gauge bits and rollers reamers)
    •   Control BHA designs through MOC process
    •  Reaming before off-bottom connections
    •   Raise rig site stuck pipe awareness

High overbalance and the potential for differential sticking can be expected due to the presence of steep
pressure ramps within the overburden, particularly in the 12-1/4” and 8-1/2” sections where the Pore Pressure
variations are the largest.

SDX-4 experienced differential sticking while  drilling the NKG pressure ramp due to the high differential
pressure through the reservoir sands combined with the highest pressure regressions in the well. The stuck
pipe incident caused the loss of the entire section and a subsequent sidetrack.

 19.17    Directional Drilling
The well will be drilled vertically to 2600m TVDbrt where the well will kick off and build at about 2.0 deg/30m to
a tangent inclination of 34 degrees on an azimuth of approximately 278 degrees. The profile will be maintained
through all the subsequent hole sections, drilling through bedding planes of 20-25 degree dip.

The trajectory satisfies the combination of surface location and target location criteria, as well as the objective
to drill close to the “drilling window” for the Surakhany overburden. The Deep Fault is being penetrated at an
angle of 34 degrees. This is not the ideal penetration angle / azimuth for this fault (but required for the above
mentioned reasons) and hence some drilling problems may be encountered.

The use of a Rotary Steerable System in the 16 ½” and 12 ¼” hole section presents a significant advantage, as
it allows simultaneous steering and under reaming, providing smoother wellbore and potentially shorter section
duration.

 19.18   Hole Cleaning
The tangent hole angle in the 16 ½” , 12 ¼” and 8 ½” sections will be below the critical angle range (45 / 55
degrees) where hole cleaning becomes a serious issue. However awareness with respect to hole cleaning (ie.
mud properties, min flow rates, pro-active circulation points when POOH, ECD management using PWD
information, ‘cavings’ trends, etc) will still be raised and incorporated into the well planning & execution process
via having “Drill/Trip/Case Plans” for the 16 ½”, 12 ¼” and 8 ½” sections.

 19.19    Well Control
Due to over-pressured water bearing sands being common across the Shah Deniz field and the problems
experienced on exploration wells  drilled  in the South Caspian, well control awareness  will be elevated
throughout the entire drilling operation. Additional emphasis will be placed on the more critical sections (16-
1/2”, 12 1/4” and 8 1/2” sections) where rapid pore pressure increase and tight pore/fracture window will dictate
an extremely robust MW Selection and thereafter ECD management strategy to avoid a Well Control Incident.

It is essential that good wellbore finger printing practices are rigorously practiced offshore so that wellbore
ballooning can be interpreted as just that and not a well control incident.

 19.20   Under Reaming
The complex pore pressure and fracture gradient profile of SD necessitates the running of numerous tight
tolerance casing and liners. As a result the clearance of the casing/liner is frequently smaller than it is in the
subsequent open hole section.

 19.21   Casing Shoe Integrity
Lower than expected leak-off tests have frequently been experienced in the Caspian Sea. Studies have
suggested that poor cementing jobs are the root cause, leading to lack of casing shoe integrity.  It is essential
that all primary casing strings are set at planned minimum depth and not early due to lack of Kick Tolerance or



      Shah Deniz D&C                       SDX-5 Operations Drilling Program                       Rev1.04
       FINAL DOCUMENT LOCATION: http://bak-cpol.bpweb.bp.com/livelink/llisapi.dll/open/7395632

────────────────────────────────────────────
[ صفحه 154 از 160 ]
────────────────────────────────────────────
leak  off at previous shoe. Raised awareness to mud properties, ECD management, surge/swab aspect,
pore/frac prediction will be key to success

 19.22    Wellhead, Liner Hanger Assemblies and Slim Clearances
SDX-5 well design utilizes the DMS-700 FULLBORE 2 WELLHEAD SYSTEM with 36” Conductor. This system
will allow running an 18” & 16” liners inside the wellhead under BOP control.

The number of casing strings and contingency liners result in extremely tight clearances and for this reason
flush and semi flush integral connections are planned for most of the strings. The downside of this is that if a
contingent liner is run, it may assist in the current section but leads to more risk in the subsequent hole sections
due to decreased annular drilling, casing & cementing clearances, which in turn can compromise well integrity
and zonal isolation.

 19.23    Major Train Wreck
In addition to the risks discussed within this document, there could be combinations of these events (in a dual
failure scenario) that could constitute a major train wreck and a possible re-spud. The specific risks and plans
to mitigate these are being worked in the Define phase. The additional work will include detailed engineering
and contingency planning.

The non-specified risks that are inherent in all projects, such as human error, collision of vessels, casing
connection failure, third party equipment failure, acts of God and others will be mitigated through the normal
assurance process of designing and planning a well.

 19.24   Contingency Drilling Liners
             i.    16” Liner
         To be run if the 18” shoe presents poor LOT or if fault issues require setting an isolation string.
            ii.    13.3-8” Monobore Expandable
        A contingency (infant stage) that may be run if the 13-3/8” x 13-5/8” Casing has to be set shallow
          due to fault drilling issues. This option retains the 12-/4” drift of the parent casing and allows a
             better chance to provide cement isolation / integrity during the running / cementing of the 10” x 10-
            3/4” casing.
           iii.    11-3/4” Liner
         To be run if the 13-3/8” x 13-5/8” Casing has to be set shallow due to fault drilling issues.
        iv.    7-5/8” Liner
           Pressure trends and indicators will be closely monitored throughout the 8 1/2” section for warnings
             of pressure regression or ramps and the need to set 7-5/8" liner before continuing to well TD (in 6-
            3/4” x 7-1/2” hole).

 19.25   Waiting On Weather
In general the Caspian Sea doesn’t experience the type of weather that could shut down a drilling operation for
significant periods of time. The impact of most events that do pass through the Caspian Sea can be minimized
with good logistical coordination.

 20  Overview of Analogue / Offset Wells


ANALOGUE WELLS

 20.1 Inam-1
Inam-1, drilled by SOCAR in November of 1995 has very little data available. What is known is that Inam-1
was drilled on the crest of the structure and suffered 6 brine flows with little associated gas before it was
prematurely TD’ed at a total depth of 2205m MD or near the top Sabunchi formation.

 20.2 INX-1
Well was a technical failure as  it didn’t make  it into the reservoir section due to high pressure in the
Balakhany (got 477m TVD into  it). Root cause, 133/8” set too shallow and no subsequent contingency
strings available.

Key Design Features

     •  Deep conductor for pin connector (181m BML in 140m water column)
     •   Moderate surface casing (828 m TVD, 666m BML) due to uncertainty about the Akchagyl and HC
        closure threshold
     •   133/8” set half way through Surakhany with a 2.00 sg LOT
     •   Long 121/4” section with diminishing KT and traverse of a major pressure ramp.
     •  No contingency available to drill through the tight pressure window.
Result; lost 12-1/4” section and didn’t have the well capability to manage the pressure build-up deep in the
well.

 20.3 YTX-1
Drilled to a similar depth as INX-1. JNOC believe the well never entered the reservoir sequence, although
BP’s subsurface group believe seismic and log correlation show the well did expose Fasila and NKG of the
reservoir section.

Key Design Factors

     •  Deep conductor (148 m BML in 14.2 m water column).
     •   Restricted surface casing to modest depth (485 m TVD, 441 m BML), due to depth of pre-well pilot
        hole.
     •   Supplemented intermediate well integrity with the addition of a 16” liner, enabling them to get next
         string into the Sabunchi and maintain KT.
     •   Opted to set 117/8” in Sabunchi with the aim of traversing Balakhany and setting 95/8” above
         reservoir. However caught by the ferocity of the pressure ramp and had to set 95/8” just below the
        top of the Balakhany (on their geological interpretation) or only halfway through the Balakhany
       (based upon BP’s seismic rework).
     •   The exclusion of 133/8” string prior to 117/8” was apparently the result of there being no 133/8”
         available.
     •   Slimmer subsequent hole sizes and casings led to excessive ECDs, ballooning, lack of integrity
       and premature TD of the well.
Result; Lack of deep intermediate contingency casing strings compromised well integrity and probably cost
them the well.

 20.4 TDX-1
Similar to YTX-1, but shallower reservoir sequence and technically successful, although dry.

Key Design Factors

     •   Moderate Conductor (102 m BML in 21m water column)
     •   Relatively deep surface casing (796 mTVD, 743m BML) with losses while drilling section due to
        shallow conductor.
     •  Ran 16” supplementary  liner  to consolidate well  in the top Surakhany and give KT to get
        intermediate well into Sabunchi.
     •   Piloted and Under-reamed to get 133/8” well into Sabunchi (unknown  if there was a contingency
         113/4”, but 133/8” left this option open).
     •   Relatively thin Sabunchi and Balakhany aided getting 95/8” production string into the top Fasila.
Result; Sufficient contingency strings and kick tolerance to ensure technical success.

 20.5 ADX-1
Similar to TDX-1 but with thicker Surakhany sequence and slightly thicker Sabunchi and Balakhany.

Key Design Factors

     •   Relatively deep Conductor (124 m BML in 104 m water column)
     •   Moderate surface casing (692 m TVD, 566m BML) with losses while drilling section due to shallow
       conductor
     •  Ran 16” casing to consolidate well in the top Surakhany and give KT to get intermediate well into
       Sabunchi. However, compromised this by refusing to fully open bottom of the hole section due to a
        higher pressure sand, subsequently left below 16” shoe.
     •   The pressure rise in the Surakhany and exposed sand below 16” caused diminishing KT and had
         to set 133/8” well above base Surakhany.
     •   However, had the contingency of an 113/4” liner which was set (perhaps prematurely) in the
       Sabunchi.
     •   Sufficient KT to get 121/4” through tight pressure window and set 95/8” deep in Balakhany.
     •    81/2” through reservoir sequence to TD
Result; Sufficient contingency available to overcome problems with shallower than desirable 16” aided by
the thinner overall well section

OFFSET WELLS

 20.7 SDX-1, 1Z, 1Y
SDX-1 was the first well drilled to the reservoirs on Shah Deniz. The well was in a mid flank position on the
east flank of the structure and was a gas discovery. Numerous problems were encountered whilst drilling,
as follows:

    •   Tight hole in the Surakhany formation, probably due to tectonics, not recognized as such at the
        time.
    •   Higher than anticipated pressures in the Surakhany and Sabunchi formations led to several kicks.
    •  A very large pressure regression  in the Balakhany formations leading  to  drilling with high
        overbalances.
    •   Thin high pressured sand, SP1, sandwiched between two low to moderately pressured reservoirs.
    •  Two sidetracks (SDX-1z, SDX-1y) due to mechanical sticking. The  first was probably due to
         differential sticking or tectonics whilst the second was due to poor directional control leading to
        stuck logging tools and junk in the hole.
    •  Two changes of rig, one planned, to utilize newly refurbished high pressure rated rig and the
       second due to generator problems on the newly refurbished rig.

 20.8 SDX-2, 2Z, 2Y
The second well on the structure, SDX-2, was also drilled in the east flank, but in an up dip location. This
too was a gas discovery. The well location proved to be an extremely difficult area at which to drill. This
was mainly due to a tight pore / fracture pressure window and a lack of planning time. Key issues were as
follows:
    •   Only one casing string set on depth as planned.
    •   Losses and gains led to the premature setting of the 16”, 133/8” and 95/8” casings and the 7” liner.
    •  11¾” contingency liner had to be run.
    •   Severe lost circulation near to the base of the Surakhany and again at Top Balakhany, due to a
          tight pore-fracture window.
    •   Over 19,000 barrels of mud were lost.
    •  Numerous kicks, including one incidence of cross flow associated with one of the lost circulation
        episodes.
    •  BOP problems.


    Shah Deniz D&C                       SDX-5 Operations Drilling Program                       Rev1.04
     FINAL DOCUMENT LOCATION: http://bak-cpol.bpweb.bp.com/livelink/llisapi.dll/open/7395632

    •   Logging problems.
    •  The well was spudded before SDX-1 had been completed and therefore before learning from the
         earlier well could be incorporated in the planning.

 20.9 SDX-3, 3Z, 3Y, 3X
SDX-3, the third well on the structure, was drilled on the northern flank in a down dip location. It was a dry
hole. Despite the number of sidetracks this was an easier well to drill. Problems encountered were:

    •   Presence of a shallow overpressured sand led to remedial cementing on the 20” casing.
    •   Three stuck pipe incidents leading to sidetracks. All appear to be directly attributable to tectonics.

 20.10   SDA-01
SDA-01, the first of pre drilled development wells on the structure, was drilled in a mid flank position on the
east flank of the structure. Key learning’s to date include:

    •   Greater than anticipated pressure and associated gas from 750m, “Q”-4, sand.
    •   22’ cement channeling that led to flow from wellhead grout ports.
    •   Mechanical failure of simultaneous drill and under-reaming of 14.75 x 17.5” interval.
    •   Greater than anticipated pore pressure measured by MDT in top Surakhany.
    •   Greater than anticipated pore pressure and associated gas from Pre Fasila sands below SP-4.

 20.11   SDA-02
SDA-02, the second of pre drilled development wells on the structure, was drilled on the east flank of the
structure to the NW of the platform location. Key learning’s to date include:

    •   Overall excellent performance to date.
    •   22’ cement job may have channeled which led to flow from wellhead ports. Source of flow may in
         fact have been SDA-01.
    •  Hughes Christensen DOSRWD Eccentric Pad tool sustained damage when used to drill out 22”
       shoe – dedicated drill-out trip planned for SDA-03.
    •  No repeat of Ander-reamer mechanical failure as seen on SDA-01.

 20.12   SDA-03
SDA-03, the third directional well drilled on the Shah Deniz structure with 2.3km step out. SDA-03 drilled
the reservoir further updip than any well previously drilled on the structure. The pore pressure / fracture
gradient was a very tight ‘window’ at Sabunchi level although the effect of this window has been reduced as
far as possible due to the deep kick off and steeper hole angles in this well. Key learning’s to date include:

    •   Overall excellent performance to date.
    •    Drilling and directional performance with the 12 ¼’’ x 19 ½’’ DoSRWD/RSS BHA were excellent
    •   Equipment reliability was an issue in 16 1/2" section (4 Failures), 12 1/4" section (3 Failures) and 8
         ½’’ section (1 Failure) of SDA-03z. Though a modification was made on 16 1/2" section BHA,
       based on SDA-02 and Schlumberger worldwide experiences,  it was not effective in combating
       shock related failures
    •   Casing setting depth was pushed into the Sabunchi horn on this well so crossing the first pressure
       ramp. The pipe became stuck in this ramp region. This TD criteria on SDA-03 was deeper than the
         setting depth on SDA-01 and SDA-02.

 20.13   SDA-04
The SDA-04 well was drilled, logged and suspended at a TD of 6189m MDBRT in 143.7days, which
included 39.66 days NPT. SDA-04 was a complex and challenging well. This was mainly due to a tight
pore/frac window at the top of the 12 ¼” section through the Sabunchi formation combined with significant
fracture strength regression by TD. Getting the 13 3/8” shoe set just in the Sabunchi Horn, as in SDA-03,
was essential in order to ‘set us up for success’ in the subsequent challenging 12 ¼” section.

Lessons learned were applied from the SDA-01/02/03 wells to result in good performance on SDA-04,
despite drilling with a recently cold stacked rig and a very inexperienced crew.  Although not completely
trouble free, the well was successfully TD.

    •   Directional performance with the RSS continued to be good, and the number of tool failures was
        greatly reduced over SDA-01/02/03.
    •  Main NPT was associated with a remedial work at the 10” shoe, stuck wireline, and MDT sampling
        attempts.

 20.14   SDX-4
SDX-4 was the first exploration/ appraisal well to be drilled on the southwest part of the field and was
designed to target the “Known Reservoirs” as well as unexplored reservoirs that may exist below the SP4,
namely the NKP and the PK. Key learning’s to date include:

    •   Well drilled to 8-5-in x 9.5-in Section TD. All directional objectives met for specified targets.
    •   First time AGR RMR utilised on Shah Deniz. Deepest water depth system has been utilised in the
        world.
    •   First time 28” Liner run and set in the Caspian Sea for BP
    •   Deepest and heaviest set 22-in Casing String in Caspian
    •  No wellhead flows as experienced on the first three predrill wells.
    •   18” Liner run and set instead of 16” Liner to provide additional contingencies for drilling Surakhany.
    •  No stuck pipe or major lost circulation during drilling.
    •   Minimal downhole losses observed during cementing and displacing operations, with exception of
       18” which was induced losses.
    •  No contingency casing/ liners utilised.
    •   Acquired MDT Fluid Samples in “Known Reservoirs” – first time on Shah Deniz
    •  AGR RMR needs to be viewed and run as a separate technology project especially at water depths
        greater than Azeri.
    •  AGR RMR deployment procedures needed to be optimised for Istiglal.
    •  AGR SPM return line valve was initially designed as fail safe open. Unfortunately when the power was
         lost at the pump this meant that the return line contents (~55bbls) was dumped at the mudline. Valve
      was redesigned as fail safe closed during the job.
    •   Performance of BHA’s that incorporated the Rhino Reamer was a disappointment especially after the
       success on SDA-04. The relevant hole sections in this EOWR highlight the key lessons learned for
       these operations from SDX-4.
    •  Cement slumping in large rat holes was a serious issue on SDX-4. Key learning is in large rat holes
        spot a heavy pill on bottom prior to cement job and prior to drilling out the entire rat hole, do cement
         integrity test at the shoe to see if it leaks. Hence if the shoe needs to be squeezed there is a solid base
         to squeeze against.
